origin: Hand-authored against abstracts fetched from NCBI E-utilities and the arXiv API; every cited id resolved against its corpus before this file was written.
license: Questions and gold answers are original; the underlying facts are from the cited abstracts.
note: LONGEVITY AND AGEING BIOLOGY, across the whole arc the field actually spans: the hallmarks of ageing and the mechanisms under them (nutrient sensing, autophagy, proteostasis, DNA repair, mitochondrial function, epigenetic drift), cellular senescence and the SASP, comparative and model-organism biology (C. elegans, Drosophila, killifish, naked mole-rat, dog ageing), the evolutionary theory that explains why ageing exists at all, geroscience interventions from caloric restriction to rapamycin and senolytics, partial reprogramming and parabiosis, ageing clocks and biomarkers, human longevity genetics and epidemiology, and the demography and clinical translation where most of it either lands or fails. Citations are overwhelmingly PubMed — ageing biology is a life-science field — with a minority on arXiv for the quantitative slice: mortality modelling, evolutionary theory, systems-biology models and clock machine learning. Swedish items are tagged `sv`, vernacular register. This domain has an unusually high `trap` share by design, because it is unusually rich in results the popular account still repeats after the primary literature moved on — the free-radical and antioxidant story, resveratrol and the sirtuin activators, telomerase as a fountain of youth, blue-zone birth records, methylation clocks read as causal rather than correlational, and single-strain mouse lifespan results generalised to mammals. Every trap states a correction the literature itself makes, not scepticism of our own.

items.question: The 2013 Cell review that established the modern framework for ageing biology enumerated a fixed number of hallmarks. How many were there, and what are they?
items.answer: Nine. López-Otín, Blasco, Partridge, Serrano and Kroemer proposed genomic instability, telomere attrition, epigenetic alterations, loss of proteostasis, deregulated nutrient sensing, mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, stem cell exhaustion, and altered intercellular communication. The review calls them tentative hallmarks and common denominators of ageing across organisms, with emphasis on mammalian ageing, and names dissecting their interconnectedness and relative contributions as the major open challenge.

items.question: Hallmarken för åldrande utökades 2023. Hur många är de nu, och vilka tre är nya jämfört med listan från 2013?
items.answer: De är tolv. De tre som tillkom är avstängd makroautofagi, kronisk inflammation och dysbios. De nio ursprungliga finns kvar: genomisk instabilitet, telomerförkortning, epigenetiska förändringar, förlorad proteostas, rubbad näringsavkänning, mitokondriell dysfunktion, cellulär senescens, uttömda stamceller och förändrad kommunikation mellan celler. Författarna kopplar också ihop dem med de nyligen föreslagna hallmarken för hälsa.

items.question: In the 2023 expansion of the hallmarks of aging, what three premises must a candidate hallmark satisfy before it counts as one?
items.answer: A hallmark must (1) manifest with age, (2) accelerate ageing when experimentally accentuated, and (3) offer the opportunity to decelerate, stop or reverse ageing when therapeutically targeted. These three criteria are what the authors use to justify promoting disabled macroautophagy, chronic inflammation and dysbiosis to full hallmark status.

items.question: The 1990 Nature paper by Harley, Futcher and Greider is usually cited as proof that telomere shortening causes cellular ageing. What did it actually claim?
items.answer: It claimed a correlation, not a cause. The paper showed that the amount and length of telomeric DNA in human fibroblasts decreases as a function of serial passage during ageing in vitro and possibly in vivo. Its closing sentence is explicit: it is not known whether this loss of DNA has a causal role in senescence. The causal step came eight years later, when introducing telomerase into telomerase-negative normal human cells prevented senescence.

items.question: In the 1998 Science paper that introduced telomerase into normal human cells, which two cell types were used and what happened to them?
items.answer: Retinal pigment epithelial cells and foreskin fibroblasts, both telomerase-negative, were transfected with vectors encoding the human telomerase catalytic subunit. Telomerase-expressing clones had elongated telomeres, divided vigorously, showed reduced staining for beta-galactosidase, and had exceeded their normal lifespan by at least 20 population doublings with a normal karyotype, while telomerase-negative control clones shortened their telomeres and senesced. The authors present this as establishing a causal relationship between telomere shortening and in vitro cellular senescence.

items.question: If adding telomerase makes human cells divide past their limit, why did knocking telomerase out of mice not produce a straightforwardly aged animal?
items.answer: Because telomere maintenance is not the same thing as the ageing programme. Bodnar and colleagues showed in 1998 that telomerase expression in normal human cells extends replicative lifespan in culture. But when Rudolph and colleagues followed an ageing cohort of telomerase-null (mTR-/-) mice in 1999, loss of telomere function did not elicit a full spectrum of the classical pathophysiological symptoms of ageing. What they did see was shortened lifespan, genetic instability, a reduced capacity to respond to stresses such as wound healing and haematopoietic ablation, and an increased incidence of spontaneous malignancies. The correct reading is that telomere length affects fitness, reserve and stress response, not that telomerase is a fountain of youth.

items.question: Two mouse experiments tested whether raising telomerase can delay ageing without causing cancer. What did each do, and what lifespan effect did each report?
items.answer: Tomás-Loba and colleagues (2008) expressed TERT constitutively in mice that had been made cancer resistant by enhanced expression of p53, p16 and p19ARF; TERT improved the fitness of epithelial barriers, notably skin and intestine, produced a systemic delay in ageing and extended median lifespan. Bernardes de Jesus and colleagues (2012) instead delivered mouse TERT by a wide-tropism AAV vector to normal mice already 1 or 2 years old; median lifespan rose by 24 percent and 13 percent respectively, with benefits for insulin sensitivity, osteoporosis and neuromuscular coordination, and no more cancer than control littermates. A catalytically inactive TERT gave none of these effects.

items.question: Om korta telomerer driver åldrandet borde långlivade djur ha de längsta telomererna. Vad visade jämförelsen av telomerer i celler från över 60 däggdjursarter?
items.answer: Precis tvärtom. Telomerlängden korrelerade omvänt med livslängd, medan telomerasuttryck samvarierade med kroppsstorlek. Analysen pekade på att det förfäderliga däggdjurstillståndet var korta telomerer, under 20 kilobaser som hos oss, plus nedtystat telomeras, och att replikativt åldrande uppstod därefter. Flera små kortlivade arter har oberoende av varandra gått åt andra hållet och skaffat sig långa telomerer och aktivt telomeras, vilket är just vad laboratoriemöss har. Slutsatsen är att människolika, korta telomerer snarast är det som gjorde det möjligt för lång livslängd att utvecklas.

items.question: What did whole-genome bisulfite sequencing of a newborn and a centenarian genome show about how DNA methylation changes with age?
items.answer: The centenarian DNA had a lower overall DNA methylation content and a reduced correlation in the methylation status of neighbouring CpGs across the genome, compared with the more homogeneously methylated newborn DNA. The hypomethylation covered all genomic compartments including promoters, exons, introns and intergenic regions; among regulatory regions the most hypomethylated sequences were CpG-poor promoters and tissue-specific genes, while CpG island promoters showed more methylation. A larger cohort assayed on a 450,000-site array reproduced the hypomethylation, and middle-aged individuals fell between the two extremes.

items.question: How did the 2016 partial-reprogramming experiment avoid turning cells into stem cells while still reversing ageing markers, and in what animals did it extend lifespan?
items.answer: By expressing the four Yamanaka factors Oct4, Sox2, Klf4 and c-Myc in short cyclic bursts rather than continuously. This short-term cyclic OSKM expression ameliorated cellular and physiological hallmarks of ageing and prolonged lifespan in a mouse model of premature ageing, and in older wild-type mice it improved recovery from metabolic disease and muscle injury. The authors read the result as evidence that epigenetic dysregulation is a driver of mammalian ageing, since the benefit came from epigenetic remodelling during reprogramming.

items.question: In the 2020 Nature paper that restored vision in old mice by reprogramming, which reprogramming factors were used, and which enzymes were required for the effect?
items.answer: Only three of the four Yamanaka factors were used: Oct4 (Pou5f1), Sox2 and Klf4, together abbreviated OSK, and c-Myc was left out. Ectopic OSK expression in mouse retinal ganglion cells restored youthful DNA methylation patterns and transcriptomes, promoted axon regeneration after injury, and reversed vision loss both in a glaucoma model and in aged mice. The benefit for axon regeneration and vision required the DNA demethylases TET1 and TET2, which is the paper's argument that a recoverable record of youthful epigenetic information is stored in DNA methylation.

items.question: When during the C. elegans lifespan does proteostasis fail, and what happens to the stress responses at that point?
items.answer: It fails abruptly and early. Using temperature-sensitive folding sensors expressed in different tissues, Ben-Zvi, Miller and Morimoto found age-dependent misfolding and loss of function of diverse metastable proteins in all somatic tissues at the permissive temperature, occurring rapidly at an early stage of adulthood rather than accumulating gradually. It coincided with a severely reduced ability to activate the heat shock response and the unfolded protein response. Enhancing HSF-1 or DAF-16 suppressed the misfolding and restored a functional proteome.

items.question: Aggregerade proteiner brukar kopplas till sjukdomar som Alzheimer. Vad hände när man tittade efter aggregat i friska, åldrande rundmaskar?
items.answer: Man hittade dem ändå. En proteomikgenomgång av Caenorhabditis elegans identifierade flera hundra proteiner som blir mer olösliga med åldern helt utan sjukdom inblandad. De var kraftigt anrikade på betaflak, samma drag som driver aggregering av sjukdomsproteiner, och de var starkt överrepresenterade bland proteiner som återfinns i aggregat vid mänsklig neurodegeneration. Olika proteiner aggregerade i olika vävnader och cellfack. Aggregeringen fördröjdes eller stoppades av nedsatt insulin- och IGF-1-signalering, alltså samma manipulation som förlänger livet, och överuttryck av ett av de aggregerande proteinerna förvärrade polyglutaminsjukdom. Slutsatsen är att utbredd proteinolöslighet hör till normalt åldrande.

items.question: The mtDNA mutator mouse is often presented as proof of the mitochondrial free-radical theory of ageing. What did the follow-up measurements of reactive oxygen species in that mouse actually find?
items.answer: They found no increase. The 2004 knock-in mice expressing a proof-reading-deficient PolgA accumulated a threefold to fivefold increase in mtDNA point mutations plus more deleted mtDNA, and showed reduced lifespan with premature weight loss, alopecia, kyphosis, osteoporosis, anaemia, reduced fertility and heart enlargement. But when the same group measured ROS in 2005, production was normal, embryonic fibroblasts showed no increased sensitivity to oxidative stress-induced death, and antioxidant enzyme expression, protein carbonylation and aconitase activity indicated no or only minor oxidative stress despite severe respiratory chain dysfunction. Mutations also accumulated approximately linearly rather than in a vicious cycle. The authors concluded that respiratory chain dysfunction itself, not amplified oxidative stress, drives the premature ageing.

items.question: Two studies of proof-reading-deficient POLG mice proposed different proximate causes for the premature ageing. What did each propose?
items.answer: Kujoth and colleagues (2005) reported that mtDNA mutation accumulation was not associated with increased markers of oxidative stress or a proliferation defect, but was correlated with induction of apoptotic markers, especially in tissues with rapid cellular turnover, and that apoptotic markers also rise during normal ageing; they proposed apoptosis as the central mechanism. Vermulst and colleagues (2008) instead identified mtDNA deletions rather than point mutations as the driving force, offered evidence for a homology-directed repair mechanism in mitochondria linked to deletion formation, and showed that the rate at which mutations reach phenotypic expression differs markedly between tissues.

items.question: What did the 2005 heterochronic parabiosis experiment do to aged muscle and liver progenitor cells, and through which signalling pathway in muscle?
items.answer: Surgically joining the circulatory systems of young and old mice exposed the old animal to young serum. This restored activation of Notch signalling in aged satellite cells along with their proliferation and regenerative capacity; exposing old satellite cells to young serum in vitro raised expression of the Notch ligand Delta, increased Notch activation and enhanced proliferation. In liver, heterochronic parabiosis increased aged hepatocyte proliferation and restored the cEBP-alpha complex, which involves the chromatin remodelling factor brahma, to young levels. The conclusion is that age-related decline in progenitor cell activity is modulated by systemic factors.

items.question: What distinguishes geriatric muscle satellite cells from merely old ones, and which gene is responsible?
items.answer: Geriatric satellite cells lose reversible quiescence. In geriatric mice, resting satellite cells cannot maintain the normal quiescent state under homeostatic conditions and switch instead to an irreversible pre-senescent state caused by derepression of p16INK4a (Cdkn2a). On injury they fail to activate and expand, and undergo accelerated geroconversion to full senescence even in a youthful environment, so the defect is intrinsic rather than environmental. Silencing p16INK4a in geriatric satellite cells restores quiescence and muscle regenerative function, and p16INK4a is likewise dysregulated in human geriatric satellite cells.

items.question: Why do old haematopoietic stem cells fail on transplantation, according to the 2014 Nature study, and what makes the DNA damage signal in quiescent old HSCs misleading?
items.answer: Cycling old HSCs carry heightened replication stress, with cell cycle defects and chromosome gaps or breaks, caused by decreased expression of mini-chromosome maintenance (MCM) helicase components and altered replication fork dynamics. Old HSCs survive replication unless faced with a strong challenge such as transplantation. The misleading part is the persistent nucleolar gamma-H2AX seen after old HSCs re-establish quiescence: it persists not because DNA damage is ongoing but because H2AX is not dephosphorylated, owing to mislocalized PP4c phosphatase. That persistent mark also acts as a histone modification that silences rDNA genes and lowers ribosome biogenesis.

items.question: Vad menas egentligen med inflamm-aging, och varför beskrivs den som ett exempel på antagonistisk pleiotropi?
items.answer: Begreppet myntades av Franceschi och medarbetare år 2000 och betecknar att kroppen med åldern både tappar förmågan att hantera olika stressorer och samtidigt får ett gradvis mer proinflammatoriskt tillstånd. Det drivs av kontinuerlig antigenbelastning och stress, och makrofagen sätts i centrum för både inflammation, immunitet och stressvar. Kopplingen till antagonistisk pleiotropi är att inflammationen är nyttig tidigt i livet, när den oskadliggör farliga agens, men blir skadlig sent i livet, i en period som evolutionen i stort sett inte har sett. De föreslår också en tvåstegsmodell: den inflammatoriska bakgrunden är första träffen, och avsaknad av robusta genvarianter eller närvaro av sköra varianter är den andra som krävs för att en organspecifik åldersrelaterad sjukdom ska bryta ut.

items.question: What evidence links gut dysbiosis causally to ageing rather than merely correlating the two?
items.answer: The 2019 Nature Medicine study of two progeroid mouse models found intestinal dysbiosis in both, with more Proteobacteria and Cyanobacteria and less Verrucomicrobia; human progeria patients showed dysbiosis too, while centenarians showed the opposite pattern, more Verrucomicrobia and fewer Proteobacteria. The causal step was faecal microbiota transplantation from wild-type mice, which enhanced healthspan and lifespan in both progeroid models, and transplantation of the verrucomicrobium Akkermansia muciniphila alone was sufficient for benefit. Metabolomics of ileal content pointed to restoration of secondary bile acids as a possible mechanism.

items.question: The 1995 PNAS paper that gave the field its senescence marker described what assay, and what was the in vivo observation?
items.answer: Dimri and colleagues showed that several human cell types express a beta-galactosidase that is histochemically detectable at pH 6 upon senescence in culture. The marker was expressed by senescent but not presenescent fibroblasts and keratinocytes, was absent from quiescent fibroblasts and terminally differentiated keratinocytes, and was absent from immortal cells but induced by genetic manipulations that reversed immortality. In skin samples from human donors of different ages there was an age-dependent increase in the marker in dermal fibroblasts and epidermal keratinocytes, which the authors present as in situ evidence that senescent cells may exist and accumulate with age in vivo.

items.question: Senescence-associated beta-galactosidase is treated as the definitive stain for a senescent cell. What is it biochemically, and what else stains positive?
items.answer: It is not a distinct senescence enzyme. Kurz and colleagues showed in human endothelial cells that lysosomal alkalinisation with chloroquine or bafilomycin A1, or equilibrating the cell interior to pH 6 with nigericin, inhibited 92 to 99 percent of total intracellular beta-galactosidase activity, while senescent cells had three- to sixfold higher activity than young ones in parallel with more beta-galactosidase protein and greater lysosomal content. So the signal is residual ordinary lysosomal beta-galactosidase activity at a suboptimal pH, made detectable by the enlarged lysosomal compartment. Severino and colleagues added that staining tracked in vitro replicative age rather than donor age, that they saw no difference in skin cells in situ as a function of donor age, and that staining was also elevated in confluent non-transformed cultures, in immortal cultures at high density, and in young cells challenged with hydrogen peroxide.

items.question: How did the 1997 Cell paper on oncogenic ras change what cellular senescence was understood to be?
items.answer: It showed that senescence is a stress response, not just the end of a division counter. Expressing oncogenic ras in primary human or rodent cells produced a permanent G1 arrest accompanied by accumulation of p53 and p16, phenotypically indistinguishable from cellular senescence. Inactivating either p53 or p16 prevented the arrest in rodent cells and E1A did the same in human cells. Serrano and colleagues concluded that the onset of senescence does not simply reflect accumulated cell divisions but can be prematurely activated by an oncogenic stimulus, and that negating it may matter in multistep tumorigenesis.

items.question: Vad kom SASP-atlasen från 2020 fram till om hur enhetligt det senescenta sekretomet är, och vilka kandidatmarkörer gick att följa i mänskligt plasma?
items.answer: Den visade att SASP är långt mer komplext än de par dussin utsöndrade proteiner som brukar mätas, och att en liten uppsättning faktorer inte kan förklara de vitt skilda effekter man ser in vivo. Atlasen täcker både lösliga proteiner och exosomlast från flera olika senescensinducerare och celltyper. Varje profil består av hundratals till stor del olika proteiner, men det finns också en delmängd som är förhöjd i alla SASP-profiler. Tre kandidatmarkörer överlappade med åldersmarkörer i mänskligt plasma och korrelerade signifikant med ålder i Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging: GDF15, stanniokalcin 1 och serinproteashämmare av SERPIN-typ.

items.question: Is there a single transcriptional or molecular signature that identifies a senescent cell?
items.answer: No. Hernandez-Segura and colleagues analysed many whole-transcriptome datasets and found signatures specific to particular senescence-inducing stresses and to particular senescent cell types, with only some genes commonly differentially regulated, and they showed that the senescent phenotype is dynamic, changing at varying intervals after induction. The markers in routine use, constitutive DNA damage response signalling, SA-beta-gal activity, raised p16INK4A and p21CIP1, the SASP and reduced Lamin B1, are described as variable and non-exclusive. The International Cell Senescence Association consensus takes the same position and, rather than naming one marker, proposes an algorithm combining several to assess and quantify senescence, plus the SeneQuest resource for senescence-linked genes.

items.question: What is MiDAS, how does its secretory phenotype differ from the classic SASP, and what metabolic change causes it?
items.answer: MiDAS is mitochondrial dysfunction-associated senescence. Compromising mitochondrial function in proliferating human cells induces a senescence growth arrest with a modified SASP that lacks the IL-1-dependent inflammatory arm. Cells in MiDAS had lower NAD+/NADH ratios, and that shift caused both the growth arrest and the loss of the IL-1-associated SASP through AMPK-mediated p53 activation. Progeroid mice that rapidly accrue mtDNA mutations accumulated MiDAS senescent cells in vivo, and the MiDAS secretome suppressed adipogenesis and stimulated keratinocyte differentiation in culture.

items.question: In the 2011 INK-ATTAC experiment, what genetic background was used, what did the transgene do, and did late-life clearance still help?
items.answer: The mice were on the BubR1 progeroid background. INK-ATTAC is a transgene that allows inducible apoptotic elimination of p16Ink4a-positive senescent cells upon drug administration. In tissues where p16Ink4a contributes to age-related pathology, namely adipose tissue, skeletal muscle and eye, life-long removal of p16Ink4a-expressing cells delayed the onset of those phenotypes, and clearance started late in life still attenuated the progression of disorders that were already established. This is the experiment that established senescent cells as causally implicated in age-related phenotypes rather than merely correlated with them.

items.question: The 2016 follow-up moved senescent-cell clearance from a progeroid model into normal mice. What was the dosing schedule and what was measured?
items.answer: Wild-type INK-ATTAC mice were injected with AP20187 twice a week starting at one year of age. Compared with vehicle, treatment extended median lifespan in both male and female mice of two distinct genetic backgrounds. Clearing p16Ink4a-positive cells also delayed tumorigenesis and attenuated age-related deterioration of kidney, heart and fat, preserving glomerular function, cardio-protective KATP channels and adipocytes respectively, with no apparent side effects. The claim is therefore that naturally occurring p16Ink4a-positive cells accumulating during adulthood negatively influence lifespan.

items.question: Where does senescence occur in the mammalian embryo, and how does the pathway differ from damage-induced senescence?
items.answer: It occurs at multiple locations, with the mesonephros and the endolymphatic sac of the inner ear analysed in detail, and the same structures show evidence of it in human embryos. Mechanistically it is strictly dependent on p21 but independent of DNA damage, p53 and other cell-cycle inhibitors, and it is regulated by the TGF-beta/SMAD and PI3K/FOXO pathways. Developmentally programmed senescence is followed by macrophage infiltration, clearance of the senescent cells and tissue remodelling; absence of p21 is only partially compensated by apoptosis and still leaves detectable developmental abnormalities. The authors propose that tissue remodelling is the original function and the evolutionary origin of damage-induced senescence.

items.question: What made Ink4a/Arf expression attractive as a molecular biomarker of ageing in rodents, and what intervention lowered it?
items.answer: Expression of p16INK4a and Arf increases markedly with age in almost all rodent tissues, while related cell cycle inhibitors change little or not at all. The increase is restricted to well-defined compartments within each organ and occurs in both epithelial and stromal cells of diverse lineages. Caloric restriction attenuated the age-associated increase in kidney, ovary and heart, and the decrease correlated with reduced expression of an in vivo senescence marker and with less pathology in those organs. The rise could be attributed partly to Ets-1, a known p16INK4a transcriptional activator, and partly to unidentified Ink4a/Arf coregulators.

items.question: Which innate immune sensor connects the chromatin abnormalities of a senescent cell to its inflammatory secretome?
items.answer: Cyclic GMP-AMP synthase, cGAS. Glück and colleagues found that cGAS recognizes cytosolic chromatin fragments in senescent cells, and that cGAS activation triggers production of SASP factors through STING, thereby promoting paracrine senescence. Diverse senescence stimuli engaged the cGAS-STING pathway in vitro, and cGAS-dependent regulation of senescence was shown in vivo following irradiation and after oncogene activation.

items.question: What did the International Cell Senescence Association consensus paper of 2019 actually deliver, beyond a definition?
items.answer: Three things. It defined and discussed the key cellular and molecular features of senescence and gave recommendations for using them as biomarkers; it released SeneQuest, a resource tool for identifying genes linked with senescence; and it proposed an algorithm for accurately assessing and quantifying senescence both in cultured cells and in vivo. Its motivation is that senotherapy, therapeutically targeting senescence, makes accurate detection of senescent cells, especially in vivo, essential.

items.question: Sharpless and Sherr argued in 2015 that the word senescence itself has become a problem. What was their argument and what did they propose?
items.answer: They noted that the term originally described cultured cells that had exceeded their replicative limit, but has been broadened to cover durable proliferative arrest induced by disparate stresses. As a result the proposed relationships between cellular senescence, tumour suppression, loss of tissue regenerative capacity and ageing suffer from the lack of a uniform definition and of consistently applied criteria. They highlighted the caveats in interpreting suboptimal senescence-associated biomarkers, whether used alone or in combination, and advocated replacing the broad umbrella term with more specific descriptors for the diverse physiological responses to cellular stress.

items.question: Varför är det så svårt att säga om en enskild cell faktiskt är senescent? Sammanfatta vad litteraturen har landat i.
items.answer: Tre skäl som pekar åt samma håll. För det första är fenotypen heterogen: hela transkriptomanalyser ger signaturer som är specifika för vilken stress som utlöste senescensen och för vilken celltyp det gäller, och bara en del gener är gemensamma. För det andra är fenotypen dynamisk och förändras med tiden efter induktion, så en och samma cell ser olika ut vid olika mättillfällen. För det tredje har begreppet självt tänjts ut, från cellodlingens replikativa gräns till alla varaktiga proliferationsstopp orsakade av vitt skilda stressorer, vilket gör att markörerna används utan enhetlig definition eller konsekventa kriterier. Konsensusgruppen svarar med en algoritm som kombinerar flera markörer i stället för en enda, och andra föreslår att man byter ut paraplybegreppet mot mer preciserade beskrivningar.

items.question: How quickly does the senescence-associated secretory phenotype appear after a cell is damaged, and in which cell types was it found?
items.answer: It develops slowly, over several days, and only after DNA damage of sufficient magnitude to induce senescence. Coppé and colleagues found remarkably similar SASPs in normal fibroblasts, normal epithelial cells and epithelial tumour cells after genotoxic stress in culture, and in epithelial tumour cells in vivo after prostate cancer patients were treated with DNA-damaging chemotherapy. In cultured premalignant epithelial cells the SASP induced epithelial-mesenchymal transition and invasiveness by a paracrine mechanism depending largely on IL-6 and IL-8, and both oncogenic RAS expression and loss of p53 markedly amplified and accelerated it.

items.question: Did DNA-repair deficiency deplete the haematopoietic stem cell pool with age, and what did it affect instead?
items.answer: No, the reserves were not depleted. Rossi and colleagues examined haematopoietic stem cell reserves and function in mice deficient in several genomic maintenance pathways, covering nucleotide excision repair, telomere maintenance and non-homologous end-joining. Reserves held up with age, but stem cell functional capacity was severely affected under stress, with loss of reconstitution and proliferative potential, diminished self-renewal, increased apoptosis and eventual functional exhaustion. They also showed that endogenous DNA damage accumulates with age in wild-type stem cells, making damage accrual a plausible physiological mechanism of stem cell ageing.

items.question: In the 1993 Nature paper that opened the genetics of ageing, which gene was mutated, how large was the effect, and which second gene was required?
items.answer: Mutations in daf-2 made fertile, active adult Caenorhabditis elegans hermaphrodites live more than twice as long as wild type, the largest lifespan extension reported in any organism at the time. The extension required the activity of a second gene, daf-16. Both genes also regulate formation of the long-lived dauer larva, and Kenyon and colleagues argued that dauer longevity may not be a simple consequence of arrested growth but a regulated lifespan-extension mechanism that can be uncoupled from other aspects of dauer formation.

items.question: What kind of protein does daf-2 encode, and what analogy did the 1997 cloning paper draw to mammals?
items.answer: daf-2 encodes a member of the insulin receptor family. It is the key gene in the neurosecretory signalling pathway that decides whether the animal enters the reproductive life cycle or arrests at the long-lived dauer diapause. Decreases in DAF-2 signalling induce metabolic and developmental changes analogous to mammalian metabolic control by the insulin receptor, and also increase lifespan. Kimura and colleagues drew the analogy to mammalian longevity enhancement by caloric restriction, suggesting a general link between metabolism, diapause and longevity.

items.question: Two 1997 papers identified daf-16. What family of protein is it, and what does the epistasis with daf-2 and age-1 tell you about the logic of the pathway?
items.answer: DAF-16 is a Fork head, or HNF-3/forkhead, family transcription factor; the daf-16 gene is widely expressed and encodes three such factors. Null mutations in daf-16 suppress the effects of mutations in daf-2 or age-1, so losing daf-16 removes the need for the insulin receptor-like signalling pathway altogether. That means the principal role of DAF-2/AGE-1 signalling is to antagonize DAF-16 rather than to signal longevity positively. Lin and colleagues separately showed that daf-16 activity is required for the doubling of lifespan seen in daf-2 mutants, which are active, fully fertile and have normal metabolic rates, and named FKHR and AFX as probable human orthologues.

items.question: age-1 var den första väldefinierade genen där en mutation förlängde livet. Hur mycket längre levde maskarna, och vad kostade det dem?
items.answer: Allelen age-1(hx546) gav vid 20 grader i genomsnitt 40 procent längre medellivslängd och 60 procent längre maximal livslängd. Vid 25 grader var effekten större: 65 procent längre medellivslängd, 25,3 dagar mot 15,0, och 110 procent längre maximal livslängd, 46,2 dagar mot 22,0 för vildtypshermafroditer. Även hanar levde längre. Priset var fertiliteten, som sjönk med 75 procent hos hermafroditer vid 20 grader. Den reproduktiva perioden blev däremot inte kortare, utan hela livsförlängningen låg i den postreproduktiva delen av livet. Friedman och Johnson noterade själva att förlängningen troligen inte beror på att man slagit ut en programmerad åldrandefunktion.

items.question: What happened to C. elegans lifespan when the germline precursor cells were destroyed with a laser, and which genes were required for the effect?
items.answer: Killing the cells that give rise to the germ line extended lifespan. The effect required DAF-16 and also a putative nuclear hormone receptor, DAF-12. Hsin and Kenyon argued that germline signals act by modulating the insulin/IGF-1 pathway already known to regulate ageing in the worm, and that signals from the somatic gonad also influence ageing in a way that requires DAF-2 activity. The interpretation is that the insulin/IGF-1 system integrates multiple signals, including reproductive state, to set the rate of ageing.

items.question: How much did mutating chico extend Drosophila lifespan, and which two obvious confounders did the authors rule out?
items.answer: Mutation of chico, which encodes an insulin receptor substrate, extended median lifespan by up to 48 percent in homozygotes and 36 percent in heterozygotes. The extension was not a result of impaired oogenesis in chico females, and it was not consistently correlated with increased stress resistance. The dwarf phenotype of chico homozygotes was also shown to be unnecessary for the lifespan extension. Clancy and colleagues took this as evidence that the role of insulin/IGF signalling in animal ageing is evolutionarily conserved.

items.question: In the companion 2001 paper on the Drosophila insulin-like receptor, how big was the effect, and what single treatment reversed it?
items.answer: A heteroallelic hypomorphic InR genotype produced dwarf females with up to 85 percent extension of adult longevity and dwarf males with reduced late age-specific mortality. Treating the long-lived InR dwarfs with a juvenile hormone analogue restored life expectancy towards wild-type controls. Tatar and colleagues concluded that juvenile hormone deficiency resulting from InR pathway mutation is sufficient to extend lifespan, so in flies insulin-like ligands act non-autonomously through retardation of growth or activation of specific endocrine tissue.

items.question: Which genetic manipulations of the TOR pathway extended Drosophila lifespan in 2004, and in which tissue was the manipulation sufficient?
items.answer: Overexpression of dTsc1, overexpression of dTsc2, and dominant-negative forms of dTOR or of dS6K all extended lifespan; TSC1 and TSC2 act together to inhibit TOR, which couples amino acid availability to S6 kinase, translation initiation and growth. Modulating expression in the fat was sufficient to produce the lifespan extension. The extensions depended on nutritional condition, which Kapahi and colleagues read as a link between the TOR pathway and dietary restriction.

items.question: Do the classic long-lived C. elegans mutants spend their extra time healthy?
items.answer: No. Bansal and colleagues ran multiple cellular and organismal assays longitudinally on wild type and on four long-lived mutants covering insulin/IGF-1 signalling, dietary restriction, protein translation and mitochondrial signalling. Measured in absolute days, some long-lived mutants did perform better than wild type. But all four increased the proportion of life spent in a frail state. The paper's conclusion is that lifespan can no longer be the sole parameter of interest and that healthspan must be evaluated separately in antiageing studies, which is exactly the assumption the field had been making implicitly.

items.question: Det brukar sägas att nakenråttan aldrig får cancer. Stämmer det?
items.answer: Nej, inte bokstavligt. Påståendet vilade på att cancer aldrig formellt beskrivits hos arten, vilket är något annat än att den inte förekommer. År 2016 rapporterade Delaney och medarbetare de två första fallen hos djurparkshållna nakenråttor. Det första var en subkutan knöl i armhålan hos en 22-årig hane med histologiska, immunhistokemiska och ultrastrukturella drag av ett adenokarcinom, möjligen av bröst- eller spottkörtelursprung. Det andra var en tät, dåligt avgränsad tumör i magsäcken hos en cirka 20-årig hane, med positiv infärgning för synaptofysin och kromogranin, alltså ett neuroendokrint karcinom. Författarna understryker att fallen inte upphäver den sedan länge observerade cancerresistensen, men att de väcker frågor om hur långt den resistensen sträcker sig och hur försök i modellen ska tolkas.

items.question: What exactly is the claim in the 2018 eLife analysis of naked mole-rat mortality, and how much data was it based on?
items.answer: The claim is that the age-specific hazard of mortality does not increase with age, in defiance of Gompertz's law, which makes the naked mole-rat unlike all other mammals studied to date. Ruby, Smith and Buffenstein compiled and analysed a historical lifespan compendium with more than 3000 data points; Kaplan-Meier analysis showed a substantial portion of the population surviving at 30 years of age, and the flat hazard held regardless of sex or breeding status even at ages 25-fold past the time to reproductive maturity. Note the claim is about the shape of the mortality curve, not about immortality.

items.question: What molecule was identified in 2013 as the mechanism of naked mole-rat cancer resistance, and how was its role proven?
items.answer: High-molecular-mass hyaluronan. Naked mole-rat fibroblasts secrete hyaluronan over five times larger than human or mouse hyaluronan, and it accumulates in tissues because of decreased activity of hyaluronan-degrading enzymes together with a unique sequence of hyaluronan synthase 2 (HAS2); the cells are also more sensitive to hyaluronan signalling, having higher affinity for it. Proof came from removal: perturbations sufficient to transform mouse fibroblasts failed to transform naked mole-rat cells, but knocking down HAS2 or overexpressing the degrading enzyme HYAL2 made the cells susceptible to malignant transformation and they readily formed tumours in mice. The authors speculate the trait first evolved for skin elasticity in tunnels and was then co-opted.

items.question: Nakenråttan lever över 30 år trots att den är musstor. Vad sa genomsekvenseringen från 2011 om oxidativ stress hos den?
items.answer: Att den utmanar den enkla kopplingen mellan åldrande, cancer och redoxbalans. Nakenråttan har betydande oxidativ stress, men dess proteom visar ändå ingen åldersrelaterad känslighet för oxidativ skada och ingen ökad ubikvitinering. Utöver det beskriver artikeln försumbar senescens, ingen åldersrelaterad ökning av dödlighet och hög fruktsamhet ända fram till döden, samt resistens mot både spontan och experimentellt framkallad tumörbildning. Genomet visade unika drag och molekylära anpassningar som stämmer med cancerresistens, poikilotermi, hårlöshet, okänslighet för låg syrehalt samt förändrad syn, dygnsrytm och smaksinne. Arten lever i stora kolonier med en enda fortplantande hona, i fullständigt mörker, vid låg syrehalt och hög koldioxidhalt.

items.question: What is unusual about naked mole-rat ribosomal RNA, and what functional consequence was measured?
items.answer: Its 28S ribosomal RNA is processed into two smaller fragments of unequal size. The two breakpoints lie in 28S divergent region 6 and excise a fragment of 263 nucleotides that is unique to the naked mole-rat and has no homology elsewhere in the genome. Functionally, naked mole-rat fibroblasts showed significantly increased translational fidelity compared with mouse fibroblasts, at comparable translation rates. The authors could not test the causal link directly but speculate that the hidden break alters folding or dynamics of the large ribosomal subunit; the significance for ageing is that the cells produce fewer aberrant proteins, supporting a more stable proteome as a contributor to longevity.

items.question: What was sequenced in the 2015 bowhead whale study, and what categories of gene changes were reported?
items.answer: The bowhead whale (Balaena mysticetus), estimated to live over 200 years and possibly the longest-living mammal, had its genome sequenced together with two transcriptomes from different populations. The comparative analysis identified genes under positive selection and bowhead-specific mutations in genes linked to cancer and ageing, plus gene gain and loss involving genes associated with DNA repair, cell-cycle regulation, cancer and ageing. Changes were also found in genes related to thermoregulation, sensory perception, dietary adaptations and immune response. The data were released publicly to support further work on the species.

items.question: What made the African turquoise killifish usable as a genetic model of ageing in 2015, and what was the proof-of-principle result?
items.answer: Harel and colleagues built an integrative genomic and genome-editing toolkit around a de novo assembled genome plus CRISPR/Cas9, mutated many genes spanning the hallmarks of ageing, and produced stable lines for a subset within two to three months, which is what a naturally short-lived vertebrate buys you over classical models. The proof of principle was that fish deficient for the protein subunit of telomerase showed the fastest onset of telomere-related pathologies among vertebrates. They also demonstrated the feasibility of creating specific genetic variants, aimed at testing candidates arising from human genome-wide studies.

items.question: The killifish reference genome published later in 2015 reported a surprising genomic location for lifespan-associated genes. What was it, and what did the authors infer?
items.answer: Candidate genes associated with lifespan differences between turquoise killifish strains, identified by comparative genomics and linkage analysis, were clustered on the sex chromosome. Valenzano and colleagues suggested from this that short lifespan might have co-evolved with sex determination. The genome also showed several ageing genes under positive selection in this short-lived fish as well as in long-lived species, raising the possibility that the same gene can underlie the evolution of both compressed and extended lifespans.

items.question: Går det att förlänga livet på en ryggradsdjursmodell genom att byta ut tarmfloran? Vad visade försöket på turkos killifisk?
items.answer: Ja, i det försöket gjorde det det. Smith och medarbetare koloniserade om tarmen hos medelålders killifisk med bakterier från unga givare, vilket förlängde livslängden och fördröjde den beteendemässiga försämringen. Ingreppet förhindrade också den minskning av mikrobiell mångfald som annars följer med värddjurets åldrande och bevarade en ungdomslik bakteriesammansättning, med överrepresentation av släktena Exiguobacterium, Planococcus, Propionigenium och Psychrobacter. Poängen med studien är att tarmfloran hos unga individer kan orsaka långvariga systemiska effekter som förlänger livet, alltså ett orsakssamband och inte bara ett samband.

items.question: Which bat holds the longevity record among bats, how extreme is its body-mass-to-lifespan ratio, and which endocrine axis did its genome implicate?
items.answer: Brandt's bat, Myotis brandtii, with a lifespan exceeding 40 years and an adult body weight of only 4 to 8 grams, making it the most extreme mammal in terms of disparity between body mass and longevity. Genome and transcriptome analysis found unique sequence changes in growth hormone and insulin-like growth factor 1 receptors. Seim and colleagues suggested that an altered growth hormone/IGF-1 axis, possibly shared with other long-lived bats, together with hibernation and a low reproductive rate, contributes to the exceptional lifespan.

items.question: How many copies of TP53 do African elephants carry, and what did the 2015 necropsy survey find about cancer mortality and body size across mammals?
items.answer: At least 20 copies, that is 40 alleles, including 19 retrogenes (38 alleles) with evidence of transcriptional activity, against a single copy and two alleles in humans. The necropsy survey across 36 mammalian species found that cancer mortality did not increase with body size or maximum lifespan; elephants had an estimated cancer mortality of 4.81 percent versus 11 to 25 percent in humans. Functionally, elephant lymphocytes underwent p53-mediated apoptosis at higher rates than human lymphocytes in proportion to TP53 status after ionizing radiation and after doxorubicin, with Li-Fraumeni patient cells lowest and elephant cells highest.

items.question: What did the 2014 comparison of demographic trajectories across the tree of life show about whether mortality must rise with age?
items.answer: That it need not. Jones and colleagues contrasted standardized age patterns of mortality and fertility for 11 mammals, 12 other vertebrates, 10 invertebrates, 12 vascular plants and a green alga. Against the prediction that evolution inevitably leads to increasing mortality and declining fertility after maturity, they found great variation: increasing, constant, decreasing, humped and bowed trajectories, for both long- and short-lived species. The authors present this diversity as a challenge to theoreticians to develop broader perspectives on the evolution of ageing and to empiricists to collect demography for more species.

items.question: What is the evidence that Hydra does not senesce, and which features of the animal are proposed to make that possible?
items.answer: Schaible and colleagues report more than 3.9 million days of observation of individual Hydra: 2256 animals from two closely related species, in two laboratories, in 12 cohorts, with cohort age ranging from 0 to more than 41 years. Mortality rates were extremely low and constant, and fertility did not systematically decline with advancing age. The features proposed to make non-senescence feasible are a high proportion of stem cells, constant and rapid cell turnover, few cell types, a simple body plan, and the fact that the germ line is not segregated from the soma. The authors argue this falsifies the universality of theories holding that all species deteriorate after maturity.

items.question: What was Kirkwood's 1977 Nature argument about why ageing evolved, and what earlier hypothesis did he say it supported?
items.answer: He argued that mortality may be due to an energy-saving strategy of reduced error regulation in somatic cells, that is, the organism economizes on accuracy and maintenance in the soma. He presented this as support for Orgel's error catastrophe hypothesis, and as a new basis for studying normal and abnormal ageing syndromes and apparently immortal transformed cell lines. This is the paper conventionally cited as the origin of the disposable soma theory.

items.question: The two classical evolutionary theories of ageing are antagonistic pleiotropy and mutation accumulation. Which did the 2002 PNAS Drosophila experiment support, and by what signature?
items.answer: Mutation accumulation. Hughes and colleagues used recent population-genetic models that yield contrasting predictions, which earlier attempts had lacked. In Drosophila, genetic variation and inbreeding effects increased dramatically with age, which is the signature predicted by the mutation theory and arises because genes with deleterious effects of late onset are unopposed by natural selection. The authors describe this as the strongest support yet for the mutation theory; note it is evidence for one mechanism operating, not a demonstration that antagonistic pleiotropy never does.

items.question: Evolutionsteorin säger att hög yttre dödlighet ska ge snabbare åldrande. Vad hände när man testade det direkt på bananflugor?
items.answer: Det stämde i det experimentet. Stearns och medarbetare lät flugor utvecklas under olika hög yttre dödlighet och fick precis det teorin förutsäger: högre yttre dödlighet ledde till högre inneboende dödlighet, kortare livslängd samt lägre ålder och storlek vid kläckning, och fekunditetstoppen flyttades tidigare i livet. Det som gör försöket starkt är selektionsregimen, som höll selektionen på fertilitet igång genom hela livet och samtidigt höll populationstätheten konstant, så resultatet inte kan förklaras av att selektionen bara försvann sent.

items.question: Guppies from high-predation streams should, by classical theory, senesce earlier than guppies from low-predation streams. What did the 2004 Nature test find?
items.answer: A mosaic, not the predicted pattern. The same high-mortality populations that had already been shown to evolve earlier maturity and greater reproductive investment, exactly as theory predicts, did not show an earlier onset of senescence with respect to either mortality or reproduction. They did show earlier senescence in swimming performance, a measure of neuromuscular function. Reznick and colleagues concluded that this challenges the generality of the association between decreased extrinsic mortality and delayed senescence, and invites more derived theories of the evolution of senescence.

items.question: Is ageing programmed by genes whose function is to kill the organism?
items.answer: No. Kirkwood and Melov state that compelling arguments eliminate the idea that death is generally programmed by genes for ageing, and criticise the widespread tendency to interpret data in terms of loosely defined age regulation, which usually makes neither evolutionary nor mechanistic sense. They do allow one carefully bounded exception: in exceptional circumstances selection could in theory favour limiting survival, so ageing might occasionally be adaptive, but they make clear that the barriers to validating an actual instance of adaptive ageing are high. The correction to the naive claim is therefore not that adaptive ageing is impossible in principle, but that no established case supports the general programme view.

items.question: What does the quasi-programmed or hyperfunction view say ageing is, and which molecular target does it single out?
items.answer: It rules out programmed ageing but keeps a quasi-programme: a continuation of the developmental programme that is never switched off, stays constantly on, and becomes hyperfunctional and damaging, causing the diseases of ageing. The target singled out is TOR, the target of rapamycin nutrient- and mitogen-sensing pathway, which is activated in cell senescence and promotes cell growth even when the cell cycle is blocked. Blagosklonny points to the convergence of caloric restriction, rapamycin and longevity mutations on TOR from yeast to mammals, and to hypertrophy, hyperfunction and hyperplasia in human age-related disease.

items.question: Gems and Partridge argued in 2013 that the field was entering a new phase. What long-standing assumption were they questioning, and what alternative did they highlight?
items.answer: The assumption that ageing is caused by wear and tear, particularly molecular damage, with reactive oxygen species generated as by-products of metabolism as a major contributor. They point out that many recent tests of the oxidative damage theory have come up negative, which opens a phase in which fundamental assumptions are being re-examined. The alternative they highlight is the hyperfunction theory, which holds that processes contributing to growth and reproduction run on into later life and produce hypertrophic and hyperplastic pathologies. They set this against the well-established picture of a nutrient-sensitive signalling network, including insulin/IGF-1 and TOR, that controls ageing rate but whose downstream biological targets remain unclear.

items.question: Which classical claims about the evolution of ageing have been revised over the last 35 years, according to the 2018 review by Flatt and Partridge?
items.answer: They list several. Selection does not always necessarily decline with age; higher extrinsic, environmentally caused mortality does not always accelerate ageing; conserved pathways control ageing rate; senescence patterns are more diverse than previously thought; ageing is not universal; trade-offs involving lifespan can be broken; ageing might be druggable; and human life expectancy continues to rise while compressing late-life morbidity remains a pressing challenge. The core theory they treat as intact is that ageing evolves because the force of selection declines with age, through mutation accumulation or a fitness benefit early in life.

items.question: What is the grandmother hypothesis as formulated in the 1998 PNAS paper, and which other human life-history traits does it claim to explain?
items.answer: That the long postmenopausal lifespan distinguishing humans from other primates evolved with mother-child food sharing, a practice through which ageing females could enhance their daughters' fertility and so increase selection against senescence. Combined with Charnov's dimensionless assembly rules for mammalian life histories, Hawkes and colleagues argue the same hypothesis also accounts for our late maturity, small size at weaning and high fertility, and carries implications for past human habitat choice and social organization and for claims about extended learning and paternal provisioning.

items.question: Vad visade de finska och kanadensiska kyrkoböckerna om nyttan av att leva länge efter menopaus, och vad hände med kvinnornas egen dödlighet när barnbarnen slutade komma?
items.answer: Med kompletta flergenerationsdata visade Lahdenperä och medarbetare att kvinnor med lång postreproduktiv livslängd fick fler barnbarn, alltså högre fitness, i förmoderna populationer i både Finland och Kanada. Vinsten uppstod genom att de postreproduktiva mödrarna höjde sina egna barns livstidsreproduktion: barnen kunde börja skaffa barn tidigare, fick barn tätare och lyckades bättre med dem. Vinsten avtog i takt med att avkommans reproduktion minskade, och just som teorin förutsäger accelererade kvinnornas egen dödlighet när deras barn slutade fortplanta sig. Det är alltså en direkt test av att selektionen för uppskjutet åldrande klingar av när den inte längre kan verka genom avkomman.

items.question: Is it true that wild animals rarely live long enough to show senescence, so ageing is essentially an artefact of captivity?
items.answer: No, and the review by Nussey and colleagues calls this an oft-quoted fallacy, tracing its roots to the otherwise seminal works of Medawar and Comfort. Under antagonistic pleiotropy or disposable soma explanations there is no reason senescence cannot evolve to be manifest within the life expectancies of wild organisms. Long-term field studies provide what they call irrefutable evidence: they found evidence of senescence in 175 different animal species across 340 separate studies, mostly birds and mammals but also other vertebrates and insects. High-quality longitudinal field data let one test evolutionary explanations for differences between the sexes, among traits and among individuals, and indicate that genes, prior environment and investment in growth and reproduction influence wild ageing rates.

items.question: State Peto's paradox and explain why it matters for cancer prevention research.
items.answer: If every cell carries some chance of becoming cancerous, then large, long-lived organisms with far more cells and more cell divisions should have a much higher cancer risk than small, short-lived ones. The paradox is the observed lack of correlation between body size and cancer risk: animals with a thousand times more cells than humans do not show a correspondingly increased cancer risk. Caulin and Maley argue this implies natural mechanisms that suppress cancer roughly a thousand times more effectively than in human cells, and that since cancer has proven hard to cure, the payoff of understanding how evolution suppressed it is improved cancer prevention in humans.

items.question: Why, on the comparative telomere analysis, would repressed telomerase have evolved in the mammalian ancestor at all, and what trade-off is proposed for the species that reversed it?
items.answer: The proposal is that telomerase repression was a response to a higher mutation load brought on by the evolution of homeothermy; with telomerase repressed, replicative ageing then evolved as a tumour-suppressive barrier. Multiple times independently, smaller and shorter-lived species reverted to long telomeres and telomerase expression. The trade-off offered for that reversal involves the energetic and cellular costs of the specific oxidative protection mechanisms needed to protect telomeres under 20 kilobases in the absence of telomerase, so abandoning replicative ageing saves those costs. A practical implication drawn is that comparative studies of oxidative protection in ageing must include telomere length as a variable.

items.question: What origin story for damage-induced cellular senescence follows from finding senescence in normal embryos?
items.answer: That its original function was tissue remodelling. Because programmed senescence in the embryo is p21-dependent but independent of DNA damage, p53 and other cell-cycle inhibitors, and is followed by macrophage infiltration, clearance and remodelling, Muñoz-Espín and colleagues propose that developmentally programmed senescence is the evolutionary origin of damage-induced senescence, which would later have co-opted the same machinery. The supporting observations are that senescence appears at multiple embryonic locations including the mesonephros and endolymphatic sac, that human embryos show it too, and that removing it by deleting p21 leaves detectable developmental abnormalities despite partial compensation by apoptosis.

items.question: In 1994 Orr and Sohal reported that overexpressing superoxide dismutase and catalase extended Drosophila lifespan. What did Orr and Sohal themselves conclude about that class of experiment in 2003?
items.answer: That the key experiments fall short of validating the oxidative stress hypothesis. The 1994 Science paper reported transgenic flies carrying three copies each of Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase and catalase living up to a third longer, with a longer mortality rate doubling time, less protein oxidative damage and delayed loss of physical performance, and it was presented as direct support for the free radical hypothesis. In 2003 the same authors argued that although the correlative evidence is considerable, significant lifespan extensions in Cu,Zn-SOD-overexpressing transgenics tend to appear when the control flies have relatively short-lived genetic backgrounds, suggesting that bolstering antioxidant defences only helps in compromised backgrounds.

items.question: What happened to C. elegans lifespan when all five superoxide dismutase genes were manipulated, and what role was left for sod-4?
items.answer: No major effects on lifespan were seen from manipulating any of the five sod genes, and the sod genes were not required for the longevity of daf-2 insulin/IGF-1 receptor mutants either. The one interesting exception went the wrong way for the damage theory: loss of the extracellular Cu/ZnSOD sod-4 enhanced daf-2 longevity and constitutive diapause, which the authors read as a signalling rather than a detoxifying role for sod-4. Doonan and colleagues concluded that superoxide is not a major determinant of ageing in C. elegans.

items.question: Möss som saknar ena kopian av Sod2 har mer oxidativ skada hela livet. Hur mycket kortare lever de?
items.answer: Inte alls kortare. Sod2+/--möss har 50 procent nedsatt MnSOD-aktivitet i alla vävnader livet ut och tydligt mer oxidativ skada, med signifikant förhöjda nivåer av 8-oxo-2-deoxiguanosin i kärn-DNA i alla undersökta vävnader; vid 26 månaders ålder var nivåerna mellan 15 procent högre i hjärtat och över 60 procent högre i levern jämfört med vildtyp, och även mitokondrie-DNA i lever och hjärna var mer skadat. Tumörincidensen fördubblades hos gamla Sod2+/--möss. Ändå var både medellivslängd och maximal livslängd identiska med vildtypens, och åldersmarkörer som gråstarr, immunsvar och glykoxidationsprodukterna karboxymetyllysin och pentosidin i hudkollagen förändrades i samma takt i båda grupperna.

items.question: How many antioxidant-gene manipulations did the Richardson group test in mice, and how many changed lifespan?
items.answer: Eighteen genetic manipulations, under- or overexpressing a wide variety of genes coding for antioxidant enzymes, accumulated over about eight years. Exactly one of the eighteen affected lifespan: deletion of the Sod1 gene. The authors note that invertebrate and rodent studies show a correlation between increased lifespan and resistance to oxidative stress, and sometimes reduced oxidative damage, but that direct evidence is limited to a few transgenic Drosophila studies; their own survival data call seriously into question the hypothesis that alterations in oxidative damage or stress play a role in mouse longevity.

items.question: Where did catalase have to be targeted to extend mouse lifespan in the 2005 Science paper, and how large was the effect?
items.answer: To mitochondria. Transgenic mice overexpressing human catalase localized to the peroxisome, the nucleus or mitochondria were compared, and both median and maximum lifespan were maximally increased in the mitochondrial catalase (MCAT) animals, by averages of about 5 months and 5.5 months respectively. Cardiac pathology and cataract development were delayed, oxidative damage was reduced, hydrogen peroxide production and hydrogen peroxide-induced aconitase inactivation were attenuated, and the development of mitochondrial deletions was reduced. Schriner and colleagues present this as support for the free radical theory and for mitochondria as the important radical source, which makes it one of the few positive results in an otherwise negative literature.

items.question: Long-lived C. elegans mitochondrial mutants such as nuo-6 and isp-1 were assumed to live long because they make less superoxide. What did direct measurement show?
items.answer: The opposite. Yang and Hekimi adapted flow cytometry to measure ROS directly in isolated mitochondria and found that superoxide generation is elevated in nuo-6 and isp-1 mutants, even though overall ROS levels are not elevated and oxidative stress is low. The elevation was necessary and sufficient for the longevity: it was abolished by the antioxidants NAC and vitamin C, and phenocopied by mild treatment with the prooxidant paraquat. The additivity of paraquat and the absence of an NAC effect on other mutants indicate the pathway is distinct from insulin signalling, dietary restriction, ubiquinone deficiency, the hypoxic response and hormesis. The proposal is that superoxide acts as a protective signal, which reframes the correlation between ROS and the aged phenotype as a response to damage rather than its cause.

items.question: What is mitohormesis, and what was the direct evidence for it in the 2007 glucose-restriction experiment in C. elegans?
items.answer: Mitohormesis is the idea that a mild increase in mitochondrially generated reactive oxygen species triggers an adaptive response that ends up extending life. Schulz and colleagues showed that increased glucose availability shortened C. elegans lifespan while impaired glucose metabolism extended it by inducing mitochondrial respiration. The histone deacetylase Sir2.1 was dispensable, whereas disrupting aak-2, the AMPK homologue, abolished the extension. Reduced glucose promoted ROS formation, induced catalase activity and increased oxidative stress resistance and survival, and treating the worms with various antioxidants and vitamins prevented the lifespan extension, which is the direct evidence that the ROS step is required rather than incidental.

items.question: Är det en bra idé att ta antioxidanttillskott runt sin träning? Vad visade den kliniska studien från 2009?
items.answer: Nej, i den studien slog tillskotten ut träningseffekten. Ristow och medarbetare gav C-vitamin 1000 mg per dag och E-vitamin 400 IE per dag till tidigare otränade och till redan tränade friska unga män under fyra veckors fysisk träning, och mätte insulinkänslighet som glukosinfusionshastighet under euglykemisk hyperinsulinemisk clamp. Insulinkänsligheten och plasmaadiponektin ökade av träningen bara i frånvaro av antioxidanter, i båda grupperna. Detsamma gällde uttrycket av de ROS-känsliga regulatorerna PPAR-gamma, PGC1-alfa och PGC1-beta, och även kroppens egna ROS-försvar, superoxiddismutas 1 och 2 samt glutationperoxidas, inducerades av träning men blockerades av tillskotten. Tolkningen är mitohormesis: den oxidativa stressen från träningen är själva signalen.

items.question: Resveratrol was reported to activate SIRT1. What technical artefact was identified in those assays, and what happened when native substrates were used?
items.answer: The activation depended on a non-physiological fluorophore attached to the peptide substrate. Kaeberlein and colleagues showed that resveratrol enhances binding and deacetylation of peptide substrates containing Fluor de Lys but has no effect on acetylated peptides lacking the fluorophore, and that in three yeast backgrounds it had no detectable effect on Sir2 activity in vivo as measured by rDNA recombination, telomeric silencing or lifespan. Pacholec and colleagues extended this to SRT1720, SRT2183 and SRT1460: with a p53-derived peptide lacking a fluorophore and with purified full-length p53 and acetyl-CoA synthetase 1, none of the compounds activated SIRT1, though all did with fluorophore-containing peptide; NMR, surface plasmon resonance and isothermal calorimetry showed the compounds interact directly with the fluorophore-containing substrates. SRT1720 also failed to lower plasma glucose or improve mitochondrial capacity in high-fat-fed mice, and all four compounds showed multiple off-target activities.

items.question: Did resveratrol extend the lifespan of mice?
items.answer: Only under one particular condition, and not the one usually quoted. Baur and colleagues (2006) reported that resveratrol shifted the physiology of middle-aged mice on a high-calorie diet towards that of mice on a standard diet and significantly increased their survival, with increased insulin sensitivity, reduced IGF-1, increased AMPK and PGC-1alpha activity, more mitochondria and better motor function. Pearson and colleagues (2008) then tested standard-diet mice starting at 12 months of age: resveratrol produced a range of benefits, including reduced albuminuria, less inflammation and endothelial apoptosis, greater aortic elasticity, better motor coordination, less cataract formation and preserved bone mineral density, and induced gene expression patterns paralleling dietary restriction, but the mice did not live longer. So the accurate statement is that resveratrol rescued survival on a high-calorie diet and delayed age-related deterioration on a standard one without extending lifespan there.

items.question: What happened to the reported lifespan extension from Sir2 overexpression in worms and flies when genetic background was controlled, and what caused the original worm result?
items.answer: It disappeared. Burnett and colleagues found that standardizing genetic background and using appropriate controls abolished the apparent effects in both C. elegans and Drosophila. In the worm, outcrossing a line with high-level sir-2.1 overexpression removed the longevity increase without removing the overexpression; longevity instead co-segregated with a second-site mutation affecting sensory neurons. Outcrossing a low-copy-number line also abolished longevity. In Drosophila, a UAS-GAL4 line ubiquitously overexpressing dSir2 was long-lived against wild-type controls as previously reported, but not against the appropriate transgenic controls, and neither was a new line with stronger overexpression. They also found that dietary restriction extended fly lifespan independently of dSir2. The authors are careful to say this does not rule out a role for sirtuins, but casts doubt on the robustness of the reported effects.

items.question: Which single downstream component of the mTOR pathway was deleted in the 2009 Science paper that extended mouse lifespan, and what did the resulting gene expression resemble?
items.answer: Ribosomal protein S6 kinase 1, S6K1, a component of the nutrient-responsive mTOR pathway. Deleting it increased lifespan and conferred resistance to age-related pathologies including bone, immune and motor dysfunction and loss of insulin sensitivity. The gene expression patterns induced by S6K1 deletion resembled those seen under caloric restriction or with pharmacological activation of AMP-activated protein kinase, which is a conserved regulator of the metabolic response to caloric restriction. Selman and colleagues suggested therapeutic manipulation of S6K1 and AMPK as a way of mimicking caloric restriction.

items.question: Rapamycin förlänger livet men försämrar samtidigt glukostoleransen, vilket verkar självmotsägande. Hur löstes den paradoxen 2012?
items.answer: Genom att skilja på mTORC1 och mTORC2. Lamming och medarbetare visade att rapamycin in vivo även slår ut det andra mTOR-komplexet, mTORC2, och att mTORC2 krävs för att insulin ska kunna hämma glukosnybildningen i levern; det är alltså mTORC2-störningen som ger insulinresistensen, inte den livsförlängande mekanismen. Att de två går att skilja åt visades genetiskt: honmöss som var heterozygota för både mTOR och mLST8 hade sänkt mTORC1-signalering och förlängd livslängd men helt normal glukostolerans och insulinkänslighet. Minskad mTORC1-signalering räcker alltså för livsförlängning oberoende av förändrad glukosomsättning.

items.question: Which autophagy gene did the 2003 Science paper show is required for insulin-pathway lifespan extension in C. elegans, and which other autophagy orthologues were involved in dauer formation?
items.answer: bec-1, the C. elegans orthologue of the yeast and mammalian autophagy gene APG6/VPS30/beclin 1, is essential both for normal dauer morphogenesis and for the lifespan extension of a loss-of-function insulin-like signalling mutant. Dauer formation itself is associated with increased autophagy and additionally requires the C. elegans orthologues of the yeast autophagy genes APG1, APG7, APG8 and AUT10. Meléndez and colleagues concluded that autophagy is a cellular pathway essential for both dauer development and life-span extension.

items.question: By how much did ubiquitous Atg5 overexpression extend mouse median lifespan, and what other phenotypes came with it?
items.answer: By 17.2 percent. Atg5 is a protein essential for autophagosome formation, and moderate ubiquitous overexpression enhanced autophagy in the mice. The transgenic animals showed anti-ageing phenotypes including leanness, increased insulin sensitivity and improved motor function. Mouse embryonic fibroblasts from the transgenics were more tolerant of oxidative damage and of cell death induced by oxidative stress, and that tolerance was reversed by an autophagy inhibitor, which is the evidence that the effect runs through autophagic activity.

items.question: How did the 2018 Nature paper raise basal autophagy in mice without deleting a gene, and what did the same mutation do to klotho-deficient animals?
items.answer: By a knock-in point mutation: Phe121Ala in beclin 1 (Becn1 F121A/F121A), which decreases beclin 1 binding to its negative regulator BCL2. The interaction was disrupted in several tissues and basal autophagic flux was higher. Both male and female knock-in mice lived significantly longer than wild-type littermates, with less age-related renal and cardiac pathology and less spontaneous tumorigenesis. Mice deficient in the anti-ageing protein klotho showed increased beclin 1-BCL2 interaction and decreased autophagy, and their phenotypes, including premature lethality and infertility, were rescued by the beclin 1 F121A mutation.

items.question: What did the XPF-ERCC1 progeroid patient and mouse reveal about how unrepaired DNA damage connects to endocrine control of lifespan?
items.answer: That genotoxic stress suppresses the somatotroph axis. A patient with a severe XPF mutation showed profound crosslink sensitivity and dramatic progeroid symptoms; XPF-ERCC1 endonuclease is required for repair of helix-distorting lesions and interstrand crosslinks. The liver transcriptome of the mouse model correlated highly significantly with that of old mice, and expression data indicated increased cell death and antioxidant defences, a shift towards anabolism, and reduced growth hormone/IGF-1 signalling, a known regulator of lifespan. Wild-type mice showed similar changes under chronic genotoxic stress, under caloric restriction and with ageing. Niedernhofer and colleagues concluded that unrepaired cytotoxic DNA damage induces a conserved metabolic response that reallocates resources from growth to somatic preservation.

items.question: Ercc1-brist ger möss ett kraftigt förkortat liv. Vad hände när de sattes på 30 procent kostrestriktion, och vad hände med de långa generna?
items.answer: Effekten var dramatisk: 30 procent kostrestriktion tredubblade både medianåterstående och maximal återstående livslängd hos Ercc1-defekta möss, som annars bara blir fyra till sex månader gamla, och bromsade en lång rad accelererade åldrandedrag. Mössen behöll 50 procent fler neuron och full motorisk funktion långt bortom kontrollernas livslängd, och Xpg-defekta möss, en modell för Cockaynes syndrom, svarade likadant. Det som hände med generna var att levern hos fritt matade Ercc1-möss uppvisade en selektiv utsläckning av uttrycket av just långa gener, ett fenomen som forskarna också såg i flera normalt åldrande vävnader och som stämmer med ansamling av slumpmässiga transkriptionsblockerande skador, eftersom en lång gen är ett större mål. Kostrestriktion förhindrade i stort sett det tapp i transkription och minskade antalet gamma-H2AX-fokus.

items.question: In the 2009 Nature report from the NIA Interventions Testing Program, rapamycin was first fed to genetically heterogeneous mice starting at 600 days of age. Based on age at 90% mortality, how much did it extend life in each sex?
items.answer: An increase of 14% for females and 9% for males, reproduced at three independent test sites. A separate cohort started at 270 days of age also showed increased survival in both sexes at an interim analysis near the median survival point. Disease patterns in rapamycin-treated mice did not differ from controls, so the authors could not say whether the gain came from postponing cancer death, from retarding ageing mechanisms, or both.

items.question: When the Interventions Testing Program retested rapamycin at a threefold higher dose, what median lifespan increases did it report, and what did the authors offer as an explanation for the sex difference?
items.answer: Median lifespan rose 23% in males and 26% in females, and maximal longevity increased in both sexes. Rapamycin increased lifespan more in females than in males at every dose evaluated, which the authors suggest may reflect sexual dimorphism in blood levels of the drug. The same paper reports that several endocrine and metabolic changes seen under diet restriction do not occur under rapamycin, and that hepatic xenobiotic-metabolism gene expression differs between the two, so rapamycin is metabolically distinct from dietary restriction.

items.question: Of the four agents in the Interventions Testing Program's 2014 Aging Cell report (acarbose, 17-alpha-estradiol, nordihydroguaiaretic acid and methylene blue), which raised maximum lifespan in both sexes, and by how much?
items.answer: Acarbose: maximum lifespan, measured as the 90th percentile, rose 11% in males (P < 0.001) and 9% in females (P = 0.001). Its median-lifespan effect was strongly male-biased (22% in males, P < 0.0001, versus only 5% in females, P = 0.01), and that dimorphism was not explained by differences in body weight. NDGA raised male median lifespan 8-10% across three doses with no female benefit, 17-alpha-estradiol raised male median lifespan 12% with no significant maximum-lifespan effect, and methylene blue changed neither sex's median but produced a small 6% increase in female maximum lifespan.

items.question: 17-alpha-estradiol is an estrogen, so it is usually assumed to be a female-directed intervention. What did the Interventions Testing Program actually find?
items.answer: The opposite. 17-alpha-estradiol increased MALE median lifespan by 12% (P = 0.002) and did not alter female lifespan at all. The benefit was also much stronger at one of the three test sites than at the other two, and was not explained by effects on body weight. This is why it is described as a non-feminizing estrogen: the lifespan effect in the ITP is male-specific, and quoting it as an anti-ageing effect in women misreports the primary result.

items.question: Jag har läst att nikotinamidribosid (NR) skulle förlänga livet. Vad hände när ITP faktiskt testade det på möss?
items.answer: Ingenting. NR förlängde inte livslängden alls, varken hos hanar eller honor, vid den dos som testades, trots att en del data hade förutspått en effekt. Detsamma gällde candesartancilexetil, geranylgeranylaceton och MIF098 i samma studie. Det som däremot fungerade var 17-alfa-östradiol, som gav 19% längre medianlivslängd hos hanar när det gavs från 16 månaders ålder (p < 0.0001) och 11% från 20 månaders ålder (p = 0.007); 90:e percentilen ökade med 7% (p = 0.004) respektive 5%, där det senare inte var signifikant (p = 0.17). Hanarnas kroppsvikt sjönk omkring 20% på 17-alfa-östradioldieten.

items.question: Has the NIA Interventions Testing Program shown that metformin extends mouse lifespan?
items.answer: Not by the analysis the ITP normally uses. Metformin was not among the 12 compounds the ITP identified as life-extending by the log-rank test.
