A 2024 reanalysis of all ITP data from 2004-2022 using the Gehan test, which is more sensitive to mortality differences earlier in the life course and does not assume a uniformly reduced hazard, did find a significant survival increase for metformin, but in males only. The defensible claim is therefore a male-only signal that depends on which survival test is applied, not that metformin extends lifespan.

items.question: The 2024 Gehan-test reanalysis of the Interventions Testing Program found five compounds the log-rank test had missed. Name them and say which sex each helped.
items.answer: Metformin, enalapril and 17-DMAG (17-dimethylaminoethylamino-17-demethoxygeldanamycin hydrochloride) were effective in males only; caffeic acid phenethyl ester (CAPE) and green tea extract were effective in females only. In addition, 1,3-butanediol, which by log-rank had increased survival in females but not males, was significant in males by the Gehan test. The authors' conclusion is that tests sensitive to non-uniform drug efficacy across the lifespan should be part of the standard ITP protocol.

items.question: Caloric restriction is often said to be proven to extend lifespan in monkeys. What did the National Institute on Aging rhesus study report in 2012?
items.answer: That its CR regimen, started in both young and older rhesus monkeys, did NOT improve survival outcomes. The NIA authors explicitly contrasted this with the Wisconsin study, which had reported improved survival on 30% CR begun in adults aged 7-14 years. Their reading was that health effects, morbidity and mortality can separate, and that study design, husbandry and diet composition may strongly affect whether CR prolongs life in a long-lived primate.

items.question: How did the Wisconsin group explain the discrepancy with the NIA rhesus caloric-restriction study, and what did the 2017 joint comparison of both studies conclude?
items.answer: In 2014 the Wisconsin group reported that roughly 30% restriction from young adulthood significantly improved both age-related and all-cause survival, and argued from body weights of the control animals in both studies, compared against a multi-centre relational database of primate ageing, that the NIA control monkeys were effectively already undergoing caloric restriction. The 2017 direct comparison of longitudinal data from the two studies (survival, body weight, food intake, fasting glucose, age-related morbidity) concluded that the health benefits of CR are conserved in monkeys, and attributed the differing survival outcomes to species specificity in the optimal age of onset and in diet composition.

items.question: CALERIE prescribed 25% caloric restriction for two years in healthy non-obese adults. What restriction did participants actually achieve, and how much weight did they lose?
items.answer: The CR group achieved a mean reduction in calorie intake of 11.9% (SE 0.7), from 2467 to 2170 kcal per day, against 0.8% in the ad libitum control group, so under half the prescribed restriction. Sustained mean weight reduction was 7.5 kg (SE 0.4) versus a 0.1 kg gain in controls, and 71% of the weight change was fat mass. 218 participants aged 21-50 with BMI 22.0-27.9 were randomised 2:1 across three US centres.

items.question: What safety signal came out of the two-year CALERIE caloric-restriction trial in non-obese adults?
items.answer: Bone loss. At both 12 and 24 months, bone mineral density at the lumbar spine, total hip and femoral neck was significantly lower in the CR group than in the ad libitum group. Three participants were withdrawn for safety concerns, there were no deaths and one serious adverse event in the CR group, and within the CR group nervous-system (p = 0.02), musculoskeletal (p = 0.02) and reproductive-system (p = 0.002) disorders were significantly more frequent among normal-weight than among overweight participants. The overall verdict was that CR at the level achieved was safe and well tolerated, with close monitoring for excessive bone loss and anaemia.

items.question: Vad var egentligen huvudmålet i den första senolytiska studien på människor, den med dasatinib och quercetin vid idiopatisk lungfibros?
items.answer: Genomförbarhet, inte effekt. De primära utfallsmåtten var kvarhållandegrad och andelen genomförda kliniska undersökningar hos 14 patienter med stabil idiopatisk lungfibros, som fick dasatinib 100 mg/dag och quercetin 1250 mg/dag tre dagar i veckan under tre veckor. Kvarhållandet var 100% utan att någon avbröt, och 13 av 14 fullföljde alla planerade undersökningar. Fysisk funktion förbättrades signifikant och kliniskt meningsfullt (sex minuters gångsträcka, gånghastighet på fyra meter, uppresningstest, p < 0.05), medan lungfunktion, klinisk kemi, skörhetsindex och självrapporterad hälsa var oförändrade. Effekterna på SASP-faktorer i blodet var inte entydiga.

items.question: In the diabetic-kidney-disease senolytics pilot, how long were dasatinib and quercetin given, when were tissues sampled, and what does the phrase hit-and-run mean in that paper?
items.answer: Three days of oral dasatinib 100 mg plus quercetin 1000 mg in nine subjects with diabetic kidney disease; adipose tissue, skin biopsies and blood were collected before treatment and 11 days after it finished. Adipose senescent-cell burden fell within those 11 days, with fewer p16INK4A- and p21CIP1-expressing cells, fewer cells with senescence-associated beta-galactosidase activity, fewer adipose macrophages and crown-like structures, and lower circulating SASP factors including IL-1alpha, IL-6, MMP-9 and MMP-12. Hit-and-run refers to the fact that both drugs have elimination half-lives under 11 hours, so the senescent-cell reduction persisted long after the drugs had cleared.

items.question: How was fisetin selected as a senolytic, and what did late-life treatment do in normal mice?
items.answer: It was the most potent of a panel of 10 flavonoid polyphenols screened for senolytic activity on senescent murine and human fibroblasts driven by oxidative and genotoxic stress respectively. Acute or intermittent fisetin given to progeroid and to old wild-type mice reduced senescence markers in multiple tissues, consistent with a hit-and-run mechanism, and reduced senescence in only a subset of cells in murine and human adipose tissue, showing cell-type specificity. Given to wild-type mice late in life it restored tissue homeostasis, reduced age-related pathology, and extended both median and maximum lifespan.

items.question: Human trials show that nicotinamide riboside raises NAD+. Does raising NAD+ mean the supplement works?
items.answer: No, and the two questions have different answers in the literature. A 26-week randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial in healthy middle-aged and older adults established that chronic NR is well tolerated and effectively stimulates NAD+ metabolism, with an early hint at blood pressure and arterial stiffness worth testing further. But the 2023 critical review of all 25 published human NR supplementation studies concluded that oral NR has collectively displayed few clinically relevant effects, and named an unfortunate tendency in the literature to exaggerate the importance and robustness of the reported effects, while allowing a possible role in reducing inflammatory states.

items.question: Which blood-based biomarkers did the TAME Biomarkers Workgroup shortlist for geroscience-guided trials, and what did the shortlisting exercise reveal about the state of the field?
items.answer: The shortlist is IL-6, TNF-receptor I or II, CRP, GDF15, insulin, IGF1, cystatin C, NT-proBNP and haemoglobin A1c. It was narrowed from 258 initial candidates by four selection criteria: measurement reliability and feasibility, relevance to ageing, robust and consistent prediction of all-cause mortality and of clinical and functional outcomes, and responsiveness to intervention. The exercise also revealed the scarcity of well-vetted biomarkers for human studies that reflect underlying biological hallmarks of ageing, and the need to use planned trials themselves for biomarker discovery and validation.

items.question: Which experiment in the 2016 spermidine paper shows the cardioprotection is autophagy-dependent?
items.answer: Spermidine feeding failed to provide cardioprotection in mice lacking the autophagy-related protein Atg5 specifically in cardiomyocytes. In normal mice oral spermidine extended lifespan, reduced cardiac hypertrophy and preserved diastolic function in old animals, enhanced cardiac autophagy, mitophagy and mitochondrial respiration, improved the mechano-elastical properties of cardiomyocytes with increased titin phosphorylation, and suppressed subclinical inflammation. In Dahl salt-sensitive rats on a high-salt diet it lowered blood pressure and delayed progression to heart failure, and in humans high dietary spermidine intake correlated with lower blood pressure and less cardiovascular disease.

items.question: Is dietary restriction a universal life-extending intervention in mice?
items.answer: No. When 40% dietary restriction was applied to 41 recombinant inbred mouse strains, DR SHORTENED mean lifespan in more strains than it lengthened it. Mean strain-specific lifespan varied two- to threefold under ad libitum feeding but six- to tenfold under DR. The strains that did badly did not have low food intake or poor reproductive potential, so neither predicted the outcome, and strain-specific lifespans under DR and under ad libitum feeding were uncorrelated, implying the genetic determinants of lifespan differ between the two conditions. Results from a single mouse strain therefore do not generalise.

items.question: Om jag tränar kondition och samtidigt tar metformin, förstärker de varandra?
items.answer: Nej, i den studie som testade det motverkade metformin träningen. I en dubbelblind randomisering fick äldre vuxna (62 plus/minus 1 år) placebo (n = 26) eller metformin (n = 27) under tolv veckors konditionsträning. Oberoende av behandling minskade fettmassa, HbA1c, fasteinsulin och glukosvariabilitet. Men metformin dämpade ökningen av helkroppsinsulinkänslighet och av VO2 max efter träningsperioden, och upphävde träningens ökning av mitokondriell andning i skelettmuskel. I metformingruppen fanns ingen sammantagen förändring av insulinkänsligheten eftersom vissa förbättrades och andra försämrades, och förändringen följde förändringen i mitokondriell andning. Proteinsyntesen i mitokondrierna skilde sig inte mellan grupperna.

items.question: What did the mTOR inhibitor RAD001 do to influenza vaccination response in elderly volunteers?
items.answer: It enhanced the response to influenza vaccine by about 20% at doses that were relatively well tolerated, and reduced the percentage of CD4 and CD8 T lymphocytes expressing the PD-1 receptor, which inhibits T-cell signalling and is more highly expressed with age. The authors framed this as a first indication that mTOR inhibition may act on immunosenescence in humans, not as a demonstration that it affects ageing itself.

items.question: The Interventions Testing Program states that it publishes all results, negative or positive. Which five popular supplement-style agents did its 2013 report find to have no lifespan effect, and what was the single hint in the secondary analysis?
items.answer: Green tea extract, curcumin, oxaloacetic acid, medium-chain triglyceride oil and resveratrol, each administered from 4 months of age in genetically heterogeneous mice at three parallel test sites. None had a statistically significant effect on the lifespan of male or female mice by log-rank at the concentrations tested. The only hint was in a secondary analysis, suggesting green tea extract might diminish the risk of midlife deaths in females only. This is the ITP's declared publish-everything policy in action, and it is why a positive result from an uncontrolled or single-site supplement study should be checked against the ITP record before it is repeated.

items.question: What did 8% dietary glycine do in the Interventions Testing Program, and what else was tested in the same cohort?
items.answer: Glycine produced a small but statistically significant lifespan increase of 4-6% in both males (p = 0.002) and females (p < 0.001), including an increase in maximum lifespan, and pooled across sex it increased lifespan at all three sites. Glycine-supplemented females were lighter than controls with no weight effect in males, end-of-life necropsy suggested treated mice were less likely to die of pulmonary adenocarcinoma (p = 0.03), and none of 40 incidental pathologies was significantly increased. In parallel analyses of the same cohort there was no benefit from TM5441 (a PAI-1 inhibitor), inulin, or aspirin at either of two doses.

items.question: What did calcium alpha-ketoglutarate do in ageing C57BL/6 mice, and what mediator did the authors propose?
items.answer: Delivered as the calcium salt CaAKG it produced a longer and healthier life, and because it reduced frailty at the same time as it extended longevity the authors describe the result as a compression of morbidity in the mouse. The proposed mechanism is induction of IL-10 by dietary AKG suppressing chronic inflammation; levels of systemic inflammatory cytokines decreased. The claim rests on a series of longitudinal, clinically relevant measurements taken to relate healthspan extension to lifespan extension in the same animals.

items.question: What did the first randomised rapamycin trial in companion dogs measure, and what did it find?
items.answer: 24 middle-aged healthy dogs received either placebo or a non-immunosuppressive dose of rapamycin for 10 weeks, with clinical and haematological exams before, during and after, and echocardiography before and after. There were no clinical side effects relative to placebo. Echocardiography suggested improvement in both diastolic and systolic age-related measures of heart function, specifically E/A ratio, fractional shortening and ejection fraction. Haematological values stayed within normal ranges, although mean corpuscular volume decreased in treated dogs. The stated purpose was to justify a larger, longer trial rather than to demonstrate an effect on lifespan.

items.question: Is alternate-day fasting better than ordinary daily calorie restriction?
items.answer: Not in the one-year randomised comparison in metabolically healthy obese adults. Dropout was highest in the alternate-day fasting group (13 of 34, 38%) versus daily calorie restriction (10 of 35, 29%) and no-intervention control (8 of 31, 26%). Mean weight loss was essentially identical at 6 months (-6.8% in both arms) and at 12 months (-6.0% versus -5.3%). Participants in the fasting arm ate more than prescribed on fast days and less than prescribed on feast days, while the calorie-restriction arm generally met its targets. There were no between-arm differences in blood pressure, heart rate, triglycerides, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, insulin resistance, CRP or homocysteine, and LDL cholesterol was significantly HIGHER in the fasting arm by month 12.

items.question: Funkar 16:8-metoden för viktnedgång jämfört med att bara äta som vanligt?
items.answer: Knappt. I TREAT-studien randomiserades 116 personer med övervikt eller fetma i tolv veckor till antingen tre strukturerade måltider per dag eller tidsbegränsat ätande mellan klockan 12 och 20. Tidsbegränsat ätande gav en signifikant viktnedgång inom gruppen (-0.94 kg; 95% KI -1.68 till -0.20), men skillnaden MELLAN grupperna var inte signifikant (-0.26 kg; 95% KI -1.30 till 0.78; p = 0.63). I den undergrupp på 50 personer som undersöktes på plats fanns ingen skillnad i fettmassa, fasteinsulin, fasteglukos, HbA1c eller energiförbrukning, men däremot en signifikant skillnad mellan grupperna i appendikulärt muskelmasseindex (-0.16 kg/m2; 95% KI -0.27 till -0.05; p = .005), där den tidsbegränsade gruppen låg lägre. Slutsatsen i studien är att tidsbegränsat ätande utan andra åtgärder inte är effektivare för viktnedgång än att äta under hela dagen.

items.question: How much can a SINGLE period of transient OSKM expression change in a naturally aged mouse, and in which tissues was it measured?
items.answer: One transient period of OSKM expression was sufficient to reverse the DNA methylation changes that occur with ageing in pancreas, liver, spleen and blood, to revert transcriptional changes, especially in biological processes known to change with age, and to restore some serum metabolites and biomarkers altered by ageing to youthful levels. So a single cycle drives epigenetic, transcriptomic and metabolomic changes toward a younger configuration in multiple tissues and in serum at once. The study was motivated by how little was known about the mechanism behind partial, reversible reprogramming, which reverses ageing markers without changing cell identity, improves tissue-injury repair in aged mice and extends longevity in progeroid mice.

items.question: What is maturation phase transient reprogramming, and how much rejuvenation did it produce in human fibroblasts?
items.answer: MPTR expresses the reprogramming factors only until the maturation phase of somatic cell reprogramming, the point at which the epigenome is already rejuvenated, and then withdraws them; the premise is that full reprogramming is not required to reverse the ageing of somatic cells. Applied to dermal fibroblasts from middle-aged donors, the cells temporarily lost and then reacquired their fibroblast identity, possibly through epigenetic memory at enhancers or persistent expression of some fibroblast genes. The transcriptome was rejuvenated by around 30 years as measured by a new transcriptome clock, and the epigenome to a similar extent including H3K9me3 levels and the DNA methylation clock, a larger magnitude than earlier transient protocols. The cells also produced youthful levels of collagen proteins and showed partial functional rejuvenation of migration speed, and the authors report that optimal time windows differ for rejuvenating the transcriptome and the epigenome.

items.question: Hur länge måste partiell omprogrammering pågå för att ge effekt hos vanliga möss som åldras normalt?
items.answer: Behandlingens längd avgjorde effektens storlek, och långa regimer var effektivare än korta. Studien prövade flera långtidsprotokoll med olika starttidpunkter under fysiologiskt åldrande hos vildtypsmöss, till skillnad från de korta cykliska pulser som tidigare bara prövats i en modell för för tidigt åldrande. Föryngrande effekter sågs i olika vävnader, bland annat njure och hud, och på hela organismnivån. De var kopplade till en återgång i den epigenetiska klockan och till förändringar i metabolism och transkriptom, däribland minskat uttryck av gener för inflammation, senescens och stressvar. Författarnas slutsats är att protokoll för partiell omprogrammering går att utforma så att de är både säkra och verksamma.

items.question: What is the ICE system, what did it do to mice, and what reversed it?
items.answer: ICE stands for inducible changes to the epigenome. It was built to test whether epigenetic information loss is itself a cause of ageing rather than a consequence, taking as its starting point the yeast finding that epigenetic information is lost over time because chromatin-modifying proteins relocalise to DNA breaks and cells lose their identity. In mice, the act of FAITHFUL DNA repair, so not mutation but the repair process itself, advanced ageing at physiological, cognitive and molecular levels, including erosion of the epigenetic landscape, cellular exdifferentiation, senescence, and advancement of the DNA methylation clock. Those changes could be reversed by OSK-mediated rejuvenation, which is the paper's evidence for an information theory of ageing in which epigenetic information loss is a REVERSIBLE cause.

items.question: Is GDF11 a circulating rejuvenating factor that declines with age?
items.answer: That was the 2014 Science claim, and it did not survive replication. The 2014 report said systemic GDF11 normally declines with age and that restoring it by heterochronic parabiosis or recombinant protein reversed functional impairment in aged muscle stem cells and improved strength and endurance. The 2015 Cell Metabolism follow-up showed those claims were not reproducible and that the reagents previously used to detect GDF11 were not GDF11-specific. With a purpose-built GDF11-specific immunoassay there was a trend toward INCREASED GDF11 in aged rat and human sera, GDF11 mRNA rose in rat muscle with age, and recombinant GDF11 significantly inhibited muscle regeneration and reduced satellite-cell expansion in mice, signalling through SMAD2/3 like myostatin. The proposal that followed was to BLOCK GDF11 for sarcopenia, not supply it.

items.question: Which chemokine did Villeda and colleagues identify as an ageing systemic factor, and what happened when it was raised in young mice?
items.answer: CCL11, also known as eotaxin. Its plasma level correlated with reduced neurogenesis in heterochronic parabionts and in aged mice, and it is elevated in the plasma and cerebrospinal fluid of healthy ageing humans. Increasing peripheral CCL11 in young mice decreased adult neurogenesis and impaired learning and memory. The same study showed that exposing a young mouse to an old systemic environment, or to plasma from old mice, decreased synaptic plasticity and impaired contextual fear conditioning and spatial learning and memory, so blood-borne factors act in both directions depending on age.

items.question: How was beta-2-microglobulin shown to be a pro-ageing blood factor, and through which pathway does it appear to act?
items.answer: B2M, a component of MHC class I molecules, is elevated in the blood of ageing humans and mice, and in the hippocampus of aged mice and of young heterochronic parabionts. Exogenous B2M injected systemically or locally into the hippocampus impaired hippocampal-dependent cognitive function and neurogenesis in young mice. The negative effects of B2M and of heterochronic parabiosis were partly mitigated in young mice deficient for Tap1, which have reduced cell-surface MHC I, implicating that pathway. Conversely, absence of endogenous B2M abrogated age-related cognitive decline and enhanced neurogenesis in aged mice.

items.question: Finns det något i navelsträngsblod som kan pigga upp minnet hos gamla möss?
items.answer: Ja, och proteinet heter TIMP2 (tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinases 2). Behandling med humant navelsträngsplasma återupplivade hippocampus och förbättrade kognitionen hos gamla möss. TIMP2 är anrikat i humant navelsträngsplasma, i plasma från unga möss och i unga mössers hippocampus, det dyker upp i hjärnan efter systemisk tillförsel och ökar synaptisk plasticitet och hippocampusberoende kognition hos gamla möss. Tömningsförsök visade att TIMP2 är nödvändigt för navelsträngsplasmans effekt. Dessutom behövs kroppens egen TIMP2 för rumsminne hos unga möss, och antikroppar mot TIMP2 blockerar långtidspotentiering i hjärnsnitt, vilket pekar på en tidigare okänd roll för TIMP2 i normal hippocampusfunktion.

items.question: What does the neutral blood exchange experiment show about whether young blood is necessary for systemic rejuvenation?
items.answer: That it is not necessary. Replacing half the plasma of old mice with saline containing 5% albumin, with no young blood involved at all, met or exceeded the effects of heterochronic blood sharing: enhanced muscle repair, reduced liver adiposity and fibrosis, and increased hippocampal neurogenesis. Comparative proteomics of serum after neutral blood exchange and after human therapeutic plasma exchange showed a molecular re-setting of the systemic signalling milieu, with some proteins ELEVATED rather than merely diluted. Added albumin was not the determinant, since albumin neither falls with age nor rises with the procedure. The proposed model is dilution of age-elevated autoregulatory proteins with long-lasting downstream effects on gene expression.

items.question: In the follow-up study on the ageing brain, how did neutral blood exchange compare with the senolytic ABT-263?
items.answer: Neutral blood exchange was the more robust intervention. After a single exchange, old mice performed much better on novel object and novel texture (whisker discrimination) tests, with reduced neuroinflammation seen as fewer activated CD68+ microglia. Peripherally acting ABT-263 had limited effects on neuroinflammation and did not enhance hippocampal neurogenesis, though both interventions reduced senescence-associated beta-galactosidase signal in the old brain, which the authors take as evidence that peripheral senescence propagates to the brain. Because the exchange outperformed the senolytic, they argue rejuvenation is not simply a consequence of reducing senescence or of diluting a peripheral SASP.

items.question: In the phase II trial of allogeneic mesenchymal stem cells for aging frailty, which dose performed better on the functional endpoints?
items.answer: The lower dose. Thirty patients with a mean age of 75.5 plus/minus 7.3 received 100 million or 200 million allogeneic human MSCs intravenously, or placebo. The primary endpoint was treatment-emergent serious adverse events at one month, and none related to therapy occurred. Six-minute walk test, short physical performance exam and forced expiratory volume in one second improved in the 100M group (p = .01) but not in the 200M or placebo groups, and serum TNF-alpha fell only in the 100M group (p = .03). Immunological improvement was seen at both doses: B-cell intracellular TNF-alpha improved in the 100M (p < .0001) and 200M (p = .002) groups and versus placebo, and activated T-cells were reduced.

items.question: What did the PLASMA trial of young fresh frozen plasma in Alzheimer's disease actually test?
items.answer: Safety, tolerability and feasibility, not efficacy. Eighteen patients with probable mild-to-moderate Alzheimer dementia (MMSE 12-24, aged 50-90) received four once-weekly infusions of one unit, about 250 mL, of plasma from male donors aged 18 to 30; nine in a double-blind crossover against saline with a six-week washout, and nine open-label after a protocol amendment. There were no related serious adverse events; one patient discontinued for urticaria and one for an unrelated stroke, and other adverse events were mild to moderate and not different from placebo. The stated conclusion is that the treatment was safe, well tolerated and feasible, with small sample size, short duration and the mid-study design change named as limitations.

items.question: Vad visade AMBAR-studien, där man bytte ut plasma mot albumin hos patienter med Alzheimers sjukdom?
items.answer: 347 patienter randomiserades till skenbehandling eller till tre behandlingsarmar med plasmabyte och låg eller hög dos albumin, med eller utan intravenöst immunglobulin. Mätningarna gjordes vid start, vid månad 2 efter veckovisa konventionella plasmabyten, vid månad 6, 9 och 12 med månatliga plasmabyten med låg volym, samt vid månad 14. Vid månad 14 hade den behandlade gruppen med mild sjukdom bättre ordflöde och bearbetningshastighet än placebo (effektstorlekar över 100%, p från .03 till .001), och gruppen med måttlig sjukdom bättre korttidsminne för ord (effektstorlekar 94% och uppåt, p från .02 till .003). De milda fallen rapporterade också bättre livskvalitet. De neuropsykiatriska symtomen utvecklades som i placebogruppen, alltså varken bättre eller sämre.

items.question: Two 2022 studies of partial reprogramming in naturally aged mice reached different conclusions about how long the factors should be expressed. Reconcile them.
items.answer: They are measuring different endpoints, so they do not actually conflict. The single-cycle study asked what one transient period of OSKM expression can do to molecular state, and found it sufficient to reverse ageing-associated DNA methylation changes in pancreas, liver, spleen and blood, to revert age-related transcriptional changes, and to restore some serum metabolites and biomarkers toward youthful levels. The long-term study asked what happens to phenotype under physiological ageing, ran several regimens with different onset timings, and found that the DURATION of treatment determined the extent of rejuvenation in kidney and skin and at the organismal level, accompanied by reversion of the epigenetic clock and reduced expression of inflammation, senescence and stress-response genes, concluding that longer regimens delay ageing phenotypes more effectively while remaining safe. One cycle is enough to move the molecular marks; sustained exposure is what the tissue-level and organism-level benefit scaled with.

items.question: The blood-factor literature has argued both that young blood carries rejuvenating factors and that old blood carries pro-ageing ones. What evidence supports each, and what does the plasma-dilution result imply about the argument?
items.answer: The pro-ageing side has direct evidence: exposing a young mouse to an old systemic environment or to old plasma decreased synaptic plasticity and impaired learning and memory, with CCL11 identified as one such factor, and beta-2-microglobulin was shown to impair cognition and neurogenesis when given to young mice, while its genetic absence protected aged mice. The plasma-dilution experiment then removed the need for a young-blood factor entirely: exchanging half of an old mouse's plasma for saline with 5% albumin matched or exceeded heterochronic blood sharing on muscle repair, liver fibrosis and hippocampal neurogenesis. Together these favour dilution or removal of age-elevated systemic factors over supplementation with youthful ones, and the dilution study additionally found some proteins rose after the exchange, so the mechanism is a re-set of the signalling milieu rather than simple subtraction.

items.question: How many CpG sites make up the Horvath multi-tissue epigenetic clock, and what evidence did the original paper give that it measures something biological rather than just calendar time?
items.answer: 353 CpG sites, developed from around 8,000 samples across 82 Illumina methylation datasets covering 51 healthy tissues and cell types. The biological arguments given were that DNA methylation age is close to zero for embryonic and induced pluripotent stem cells, that it correlates with cell passage number, that age acceleration derived from it is highly heritable, that it transfers to chimpanzee tissues, and that all 20 cancer types examined across about 6,000 samples showed significant age acceleration, averaging 36 years. Horvath proposed the clock measures the cumulative effect of an epigenetic maintenance system.

items.question: How does the Hannum clock differ from the Horvath clock in the data it was built on?
items.answer: The Hannum model was built from a single tissue, whole blood, using more than 450,000 CpG markers in 656 individuals aged 19 to 101, and was framed as a quantitative model of the RATE at which an individual's methylome ages, shown to be influenced by sex and by genetic variants. The Horvath predictor was built from around 8,000 samples spanning 51 healthy tissues and cell types across 82 datasets and reduced to 353 CpGs, so it is explicitly multi-tissue and applicable where blood is not available. Both were tested beyond their training data: Hannum's model was shown to hold in other human tissues and to reveal advanced ageing rate in tumour tissue, Horvath's showed significant age acceleration in all 20 cancer types examined.

items.question: Vad är det egentligen DNAm PhenoAge är tränad på, och varför spelar det roll?
items.answer: Den är tränad mot ett sammansatt kliniskt mått på fenotypisk ålder, inte mot kalenderålder. Den första generationens epigenetiska klockor använde kalenderålder som ersättning för biologisk ålder; PhenoAge byggdes i stället i två steg, där ett kliniskt mått som fångar skillnader i livslängd och hälsospann först togs fram och en DNA-metyleringsmodell sedan tränades mot det. Det gör att den slår tidigare mått på en rad utfall: total dödlighet, cancer, hälsospann, fysisk funktion och Alzheimers sjukdom. Måttet togs fram i helblod men korrelerar starkt med ålder i alla vävnader och celltyper som prövats. Förhöjd epigenetisk ålder i förhållande till kalenderålder följdes av ökad aktivering av proinflammatoriska vägar och interferonvägar och minskad aktivering av transkriptions- och translationsmaskineri, DNA-skadesvar och mitokondriella signaturer.

items.question: What is DNAm GrimAge actually composed of?
items.answer: It is a composite of seven DNA methylation based surrogate estimators of plasma proteins, including plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 (PAI-1) and growth differentiation factor 15, plus a DNA methylation based estimator of smoking pack-years. The composite is expressed in units of years, and adjusting it for chronological age gives the age-acceleration measure AgeAccelGrim. In validation across thousands of individuals it stood out among existing clocks for predicting time to death (Cox P = 2.0E-75), time to coronary heart disease (P = 6.2E-24) and time to cancer (P = 1.3E-12), and correlated with CT-measured fatty liver and visceral fat and with age at menopause.

items.question: If two people both have accelerated biological age, does it matter which measure was used to say so?
items.answer: Yes, because the measures do not agree with one another. Eleven quantifications of biological ageing (telomere length and erosion, three epigenetic clocks and their ticking rates, and three biomarker composites) were implemented on the SAME 964 middle-aged people in the Dunedin cohort, and agreement between them was low, contrary to expectation. Only the 71-CpG epigenetic clock and the biomarker composites were consistently related to the outcomes geroprotective therapies aim at (physical functioning, cognitive decline, subjective signs of ageing including facial appearance), and even there the effect sizes were modest. The authors' conclusion is that different proposed approaches may not be measuring the same aspect of ageing at all, so a result stated as accelerated biological ageing is only interpretable together with the instrument that produced it.

items.question: What did GrimAge version 2 add to the original GrimAge, and what did it buy?
items.answer: Two new DNA methylation based estimators of log-transformed plasma proteins: high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (logCRP) and haemoglobin A1c (logA1C). Evaluated in 13,399 blood samples across nine cohorts and adjusted for age and sex, GrimAge2 outperformed GrimAge for mortality prediction across multiple racial and ethnic groups (meta P = 3.6E-167 versus 2.6E-144), and related to coronary heart disease, to FEV1 (correlation -0.31) and to CT measures of fatty liver disease. It was also shown to apply to younger individuals and to saliva samples. DNAm logA1C was highly associated with type 2 diabetes and DNAm PAI-1 outperformed the other age-adjusted markers, including GrimAge2, for triglycerides and visceral fat.

items.question: What makes DunedinPACE different in construction from a clock like PhenoAge or GrimAge?
items.answer: It estimates a RATE rather than an age. It was modelled on within-individual decline in 19 indicators of organ-system integrity measured at four time points spanning two decades in the Dunedin 1972-1973 birth cohort, and that two-decade Pace of Aging was then distilled into a single-time-point blood test by elastic-net regression, on a methylation dataset restricted to exclude probes with low test-retest reliability. In five further datasets DunedinPACE showed high test-retest reliability and associations with morbidity, disability and mortality, indicated faster ageing in young adults who had experienced childhood adversity, had effect sizes similar to GrimAge, and added incremental prediction beyond GrimAge for incident morbidity, disability and mortality.

items.question: How reproducible is a single epigenetic-clock reading from one person's blood?
items.answer: Much less than the reported precision suggests. Technical noise produced deviations of up to 9 years between replicate samples for six prominent epigenetic clocks, which limits their use for individual readings, longitudinal tracking and intervention trials. The proposed fix is computational rather than experimental: calculate principal components from CpG-level data and use those as input to the age predictor. Retrained principal-component versions of the same six clocks agreed between most replicates within 1.5 years, improved detection of clock associations and of intervention effects, and gave reliable longitudinal trajectories in vivo and in vitro. The method adds one step, needs no replicates or prior knowledge of CpG reliabilities in training, and can be applied to any existing or future epigenetic biomarker.

items.question: Om min DNA-metyleringsålder ligger fem år över min kalenderålder, vad innebär det?
items.answer: I en metaanalys av fyra longitudinella kohorter av äldre människor var fem års högre metyleringsålder kopplad till 21% högre risk att dö, justerat för ålder och kön. Efter ytterligare justering för barndoms-IQ, utbildning, samhällsklass, högt blodtryck, diabetes, hjärt-kärlsjukdom och APOE e4-status kvarstod 16% högre risk, alltså oberoende av hälsotillstånd, livsstilsfaktorer och kända genetiska faktorer. Skillnaden mellan metyleringsålder och kalenderålder är dessutom ärftlig: en separat släktbaserad analys gav en ärftlighet på 0.43. Det handlar om en riskökning skattad på gruppnivå, inte om en prognos för en enskild människa.

items.question: When methylation clocks were applied to the CALERIE caloric-restriction trial, which measure moved and which did not?
items.answer: DunedinPACE moved; the age-style clocks did not. In a post hoc analysis of blood from the 220 non-obese adults randomised to 25% caloric restriction or ad libitum diet for two years, the intervention slowed the pace of ageing as measured by DunedinPACE, but did not produce significant changes in biological age estimates from clocks including PhenoAge and GrimAge. Treatment effect sizes were small. The authors read this as support for the geroscience hypothesis from a randomised trial rather than from small uncontrolled studies, while noting that a conclusive test needs long-term follow-up to primary healthy-ageing endpoints such as chronic-disease incidence and mortality.

items.question: In the TILDA cohort comparison of four epigenetic clocks against clinical phenotypes, which clocks predicted health and which did not?
items.answer: In 490 participants of the Irish Longitudinal Study on Ageing followed up to 10 years, Horvath and Hannum age acceleration were not predictive of health at all. PhenoAge acceleration was associated with 4 of 9 outcomes (walking speed, frailty, MOCA, MMSE) in minimally adjusted models but not once social and lifestyle factors were included. GrimAge acceleration was associated with 8 of 9 outcomes, all except grip strength, in minimally adjusted models, and remained a significant predictor of walking speed, polypharmacy, frailty and all-cause mortality in fully adjusted models. The nine outcomes were walking speed, grip strength, Fried frailty, polypharmacy, MMSE, MOCA, sustained attention reaction time and two-choice reaction time, plus mortality.

items.question: What is a transcriptomic age, and on what scale of data was the first blood-based one built?
items.answer: It is an age prediction from whole-blood gene expression rather than from methylation. The meta-analysis behind it covered 14,983 individuals of European ancestry including replication and identified 1,497 genes differentially expressed with chronological age. Those age-associated genes did not carry more age-associated CpG methylation sites than other genes, but were enriched for potentially functional CpG methylation sites in enhancer and insulator regions associated with both age and expression level. The gap between transcriptomic age and chronological age was associated with blood pressure, cholesterol, fasting glucose and body mass index, and the authors present the model as complementing rather than replacing epigenetic predictors.

items.question: What do plasma-proteomic organ-specific ageing models add over a single whole-body clock, and what sex difference did they show?
items.answer: They resolve ageing by organ and system rather than giving one number. Built by elastic-net regularisation on plasma proteome data from over 50,000 UK Biobank subjects and other cohorts, and trained on chronological age, on mortality and on longitudinal proteome data, they predict organ- and system-specific disease. Men were found to age faster than women in most organs. Accelerated ageing of a given organ led to disease in that organ, and specific diets, lifestyles, professions and medications influenced organ ageing rates, with the driving proteins identified. The framing is that age-related chronic diseases epitomise accelerated organ-specific ageing, which argues for personalised organ-targeted interventions alongside whole-organism ones.

items.question: What did the largest GWAS of epigenetic-clock measures find, and what was surprising about where the loci sat?
items.answer: Using methylation and SNP data from more than 40,000 individuals, GWAS meta-analyses of four epigenetic clocks plus epigenetic surrogates for granulocyte proportion and PAI-1 identified 137 genome-wide significant loci, of which 113 were novel. Loci shared with the Horvath clock included expression of transcripts for genes linked to lipid metabolism and immune function. The notable point is that these loci were INDEPENDENT of those already reported to regulate methylation levels at the constituent clock CpGs, so the genetics of clock acceleration is not simply the genetics of methylation at the clock sites. A polygenic score for GrimAge acceleration was strongly associated with adiposity traits, educational attainment, parental longevity and C-reactive protein.

items.question: Hur räknar man ut ett skörhetsindex, ett frailty index, och vad har det för egenskaper?
items.answer: Som andelen av de möjliga bristerna som en person faktiskt har. Symtom, tecken, sjukdomar och funktionsnedsättningar räknas alla som brister och summeras i ett index, och poängen speglar hur stor andel av de tänkbara bristerna som finns hos just den personen och därmed hur sannolikt det är att skörhet föreligger. Trots att det bara är en uppräkning har indexet flera intressanta egenskaper: en karakteristisk ackumulationstakt, en submaximal gräns som i praktiken inte överskrids, och en karakteristisk förändring av fördelningen med stigande ålder. Det fungerar som en tillståndsvariabel som kvantitativt sammanfattar sårbarhet, där skörhet ses som en åldersrelaterad och ospecifik sårbarhet snarare än en enskild sjukdom.

items.question: What does an epigenetic clock reading not tell you about an individual?
items.answer: Two limits are documented. First, agreement between measures is poor: eleven telomere, epigenetic-clock and biomarker-composite quantifications applied to the same 964 people showed low agreement, and only some of them related to physical functioning, cognitive decline and subjective signs of ageing, with modest effect sizes even then. Second, the clocks differ sharply from one another in predictive value: in 490 TILDA participants, Horvath and Hannum age acceleration were not predictive of any clinical phenotype, PhenoAge acceleration lost its associations once social and lifestyle factors were adjusted for, and only GrimAge acceleration survived full adjustment, and only for walking speed, polypharmacy, frailty and mortality. So a clock number is a population-level risk indicator tied to the specific algorithm used, not a personal statement of how much biological ageing has occurred.

items.question: What did the 40-month metformin study in male cynomolgus monkeys measure, and what was the headline effect?
items.answer: It combined physiological, imaging, histological and molecular evaluation with purpose-built monkey ageing clocks derived from pan-tissue transcriptomics, DNA methylomics, plasma proteomics and metabolomics, and used those clocks to gauge the drug's effect. Metformin slowed the ageing indicators, with the headline being roughly a 6-year regression in brain ageing, together with preserved brain structure and improved cognitive ability. The neuroprotective effect on primate neurons was partly mediated by activation of Nrf2. The claim is a reduction in multi-dimensional biological age in a primate, measured by clocks, not a demonstrated effect on lifespan.

items.question: What is the difference between a clock trained on chronological age and one trained on a phenotype, and what does that difference imply about how each should be read?
items.answer: The first generation, of which the 353-CpG multi-tissue predictor is the reference, was trained to predict calendar age using chronological age as a surrogate for biological age, so its residual against calendar age is a derived quantity rather than the thing it optimised. The second generation was trained on something else entirely: DNAm PhenoAge was built in two steps around a composite clinical measure of phenotypic age capturing lifespan and healthspan differences, and outperforms the first generation on mortality, cancer, healthspan, physical functioning and Alzheimer's disease. The practical implication is that a first-generation clock is best read as an accurate age estimator whose deviations are noisy indicators, while a phenotype- or mortality-trained clock is read as a risk score, and the two are not interchangeable inputs to a trial endpoint.

items.question: What was the effect size for the FOXO3A longevity association in the 2008 study of long-lived men of Japanese ancestry, and how was the study designed to avoid the usual pitfalls?
items.answer: The odds ratio comparing homozygous minor with homozygous major allele carriers between cases and controls was 2.75 (P = 0.00009; adjusted P = 0.00135). The design chose a large, homogeneous, long-lived population of men well characterised for ageing phenotypes and ran a nested case-control study of five candidate genes in the insulin/IGF-1 signalling pathway, precisely to avoid the small samples, imprecise phenotyping and population stratification that had hampered earlier attempts. The long-lived men also had lower prevalence of cancer and cardiovascular disease, better self-reported health, high physical and cognitive function, and markers of greater insulin sensitivity associated with the FOXO3A GG genotype.

items.question: Long life is commonly said to be 15-30% heritable. What did the analysis of very large pedigree data conclude?
items.answer: That the usual figure is substantially inflated. Using pedigree data from Ancestry public trees covering hundreds of millions of historical persons, nominal heritability estimates based on correlations among genetic relatives agreed with the prior literature, but the majority of that correlation was ALSO captured by correlations among non-genetic in-law relatives, which points to highly assortative mating around lifespan-influencing factors. After accounting for assortative mating with structural equation modelling, the true heritability of human longevity for birth cohorts across the 1800s and early 1900s was well below 10%. The 15-30% figure is therefore an artefact of who marries whom, not a measure of transmitted genetics.

items.question: Which variants reached genome-wide significance in the 2019 longevity GWAS meta-analysis, and in which direction did each act?
items.answer: Three. rs429358, the APOE epsilon-4 allele, was associated with LOWER odds of surviving to the 90th and 99th percentile age. rs7412, the APOE epsilon-2 allele, showed the opposite direction. And rs7676745, located near GPR78, associated with lower odds of surviving to the 90th percentile age. Gene-level analysis additionally implicated tissue-specific expression of multiple genes in longevity, and genetic correlation with disease-related phenotypes pointed to a shared architecture between health and longevity.

items.question: Hur definierade Deelen och medarbetare 2019 vem som räknas som långlivad i sin GWAS-metaanalys?
items.answer: Med en relativ, överlevnadsbaserad definition i stället för en fast åldersgräns. Fall var personer som överlevde till eller bortom den ålder som motsvarar 90:e respektive 99:e överlevnadspercentilen, vilket gav 11 262 fall för 90:e percentilen och 3 484 för 99:e. Kontroller var personer vars dödsålder eller ålder vid senaste kontakt låg vid eller under den ålder som motsvarar 60:e överlevnadspercentilen, totalt 25 483 personer. Två separata metaanalyser kördes, en för varje falldefinition. Poängen med att förankra gränserna i överlevnadspercentiler är att en och samma kalenderålder betyder olika saker i olika befolkningar och födelsekohorter, så en fast gräns som till exempel 90 år skulle blanda ihop verkligt exceptionell överlevnad med vanlig.

items.question: Before informed GWAS was applied, how many loci reached significance for exceptional human longevity in the two study cohorts, and what was the idea behind the informed method?
items.answer: In a standard GWAS analysis of those two studies of long-lived humans, only ONE locus was significant at a 10% false discovery rate: APOE/TOMM40. The informed GWAS method (iGWAS) takes prior knowledge from large studies of age-related DISEASE and uses it to narrow the search for longevity-associated SNPs, motivated by the demonstrated overlap between disease loci and extreme-longevity loci, with several disease variants apparently depleted in centenarians relative to the general population. Drawing on 14 meta-analyses of disease and trait GWAS, iGWAS raised the count to eight loci significant at FDR below 10%.

items.question: Which longevity loci replicated in independent cohorts in the informed-GWAS study, and what is each known for?
items.answer: Four replicated at FDR below 5%, with suggestive evidence for one more. They were APOE/TOMM40, associated with Alzheimer's disease; CDKN2B/ANRIL, implicated in the regulation of cellular senescence; ABO, which tags the O blood group; and SH2B3/ATXN2, a signalling gene that extends lifespan in Drosophila and is involved in neurological disease. The pattern was taken as evidence of genetic overlap between longevity and age-related diseases and traits including coronary artery disease and Alzheimer's disease.

items.question: A 2010 Science paper reported a 150-SNP genetic signature that predicted exceptional longevity with 77% accuracy. Can that model be used?
items.answer: No. The paper was RETRACTED. As published it reported a genome-wide association study of exceptional longevity in 1055 centenarians and 1267 controls, a 150-SNP model said to predict exceptional longevity with 77% accuracy in an independent set, and 19 genetic signature clusters covering 90% of centenarians and correlating with prevalence and age of onset of dementia, hypertension and cardiovascular disease. Its retraction is the reason later work reports so few genome-wide significant longevity loci: subsequent properly powered meta-analyses recover essentially APOE plus a handful of others, not a high-accuracy multi-SNP predictor. Any answer that cites the 77% figure as a current result is citing withdrawn work.

items.question: What lipoprotein phenotype and which CETP genotype were associated with exceptional longevity in the Ashkenazi centenarian study?
items.answer: Larger HDL and LDL particle sizes, measured by proton NMR, significantly higher in the 213 probands of mean age 98.2 than in either control group (P = .001), independent of plasma HDL and LDL cholesterol and of apolipoprotein A1 and B levels. The genotype was homozygosity for the valine allele of the codon 405 isoleucine-to-valine (I405V) variant in the cholesteryl ester transfer protein gene: probands and offspring had 2.9-fold and 3.6-fold higher frequency of the VV genotype in men, and 2.7-fold and 1.5-fold in women, than controls (P < .001). Probands with the VV genotype had larger lipoprotein particles and lower serum CETP concentrations.

items.question: The FOXO3 rs2802292 G allele is associated with longevity across populations. Which cause of death actually drives the survival advantage?
items.answer: Coronary heart disease. In a 17-year prospective study of 3584 older American men of Japanese ancestry from the Honolulu Heart Program, replicated in 1595 white and 1056 black participants of the Health Aging and Body Composition cohort, G allele carriers had a combined 10% reduction in all-cause mortality (HR 0.90; 95% CI 0.84-0.95; P = 0.001). That was mostly contributed by a 26% lower risk of death from coronary heart disease (HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.64-0.86; P = 0.00004). No other cause of death, including cancer or stroke, made a significant contribution.

items.question: Stämmer det att kortare män lever längre?
items.answer: I den kohort där saken undersöktes noggrant pekar data åt det hållet, men effekten per centimeter är liten. I Honolulu Heart Program och Honolulu-Asia Aging Study följdes 8 003 amerikanska män av japansk härkomst i över 40 år. Kroppslängd i medelåldern var positivt kopplad till total dödlighet, RR 1.007 per enhet ökad längd (95% KI 1.003-1.011; p = 0.002), och justering för tänkbara störfaktorer ändrade det bara marginellt (RR 1.006; p = 0.007). Längd var också positivt kopplad till cancerdöd och till dödlighet i cancer utan koppling till rökning, och den relativa risken ökade med stigande ålder i kohorten. Den långlivadhetsassocierade FOXO3-varianten var omvänt kopplad till längd, och längd var positivt kopplad till fasteinsulin, vilket författarna tolkar som stöd för att insulin- och IGF-1-signaleringen är den underliggande mekanismen snarare än längden i sig.

items.question: On what data are current estimates of sibling relative risk for exceptional longevity based, and what does the accompanying model let you compute?
items.answer: On more than 1,700 sibships, used to update estimates of the relative risk of a sibling of a long-lived person also living to extreme age, together with an examination of how heritability trends across different birth-year cohorts. The accompanying network model spans familial longevity across three generations and computes an individual's increased chance of exceptional longevity conditional on their family history, including the separate effects of paternal and maternal longevity. The motivation given is that mortality risk assessment normally ignores familial longevity information entirely.

items.question: How long has the Okinawa Centenarian Study been running, how does it define a centenarian, and how many have been examined?
items.answer: It began in 1975 as a population-based study of centenarians and other selected elderly people living on the main island of Okinawa prefecture, and by 2015 had examined over 1000 centenarians, so more than four decades of continuous work. Note the definition used: the study counts 99-year-olds and older as centenarians, not only those who have passed 100. The research group's summary position is that by several measures of health and longevity the Okinawans can claim to be the world's healthiest and longest-lived people.

items.question: The Sardinian blue zone is usually presented as a validated example of a long-lived population. What did the study that identified it actually say about validation?
items.answer: It said the opposite of what the popular account implies. The AKEA study defined an extreme longevity index from the percentage of people born in Sardinia between 1880 and 1900 who reached 100, and used gaussian smoothing to locate a blue zone in the mountainous central-eastern part of the island, where the male-to-female ratio among centenarians was 1.35 against 2.43 in the rest of Sardinia. But the authors state explicitly that although longevity hot spots have been identified in various regions of the world over the years, NONE of these longevity regions had been fully validated, and they name Sardinia's low female-to-male ratio among validated centenarians as what makes their own case unusual. They also offer inbreeding, through frequent consanguineous marriage and low immigration, as an alternative explanation to any lifestyle account.

items.question: What happened when parental lifespan was used as the phenotype in a genome-wide association study in the Health and Retirement Study?
items.answer: The lead signal failed to replicate. A genome-wide significant association was found for rs35715456 on chromosome 18 (log10 Bayes factor 6.3) for the dichotomous trait of having at least one long-lived parent versus none, but that association was not replicated in independent samples from InCHIANTI and the Framingham Heart Study. Among SNPs in established longevity candidate genes (APOE, MINIPP1, FOXO3, EBF1, CAMKIV, OTOL1) the most significant association was in the EBF1 gene region (rs17056207, p = .0002). The result is reported as a promising signal that did not hold, which is the normal outcome for lifespan GWAS at this sample size.

items.question: Vad hade barnen till de exceptionellt långlivade i den judiska hundraåringsstudien gemensamt med sina föräldrar?
items.answer: Fenotypen med stora lipoproteinpartiklar. Både probanderna, 213 personer med en medelålder på 98.2 år, och deras 216 barn med en medelålder på 68.3 år hade signifikant större HDL- och LDL-partiklar än åldersmatchade kontroller, oberoende av plasmanivåerna av HDL- och LDL-kolesterol och av apolipoprotein A1 och B. Barnen delade alltså fenotypen, medan kontrollerna inte gjorde det. Både barnen och kontrollerna hade större partiklar om de var fria från högt blodtryck, hjärt-kärlsjukdom eller metabolt syndrom. Barnen hade också en klart högre frekvens av homozygoti för valinallelen i CETP-varianten I405V, 3.6 gånger hos män och 1.5 gånger hos kvinnor jämfört med kontroller.

items.question: What does the genetic architecture of human longevity look like once modern GWAS are taken together, and why does so little of it survive?
items.answer: It is dominated by APOE with a thin tail behind it. The 2019 meta-analysis using survival-percentile case definitions found rs429358 (epsilon-4, reducing odds of survival), rs7412 (epsilon-2, the opposite) and rs7676745 near GPR78, plus gene-level evidence for tissue-specific expression of multiple genes, and genetic correlation with disease phenotypes indicating a shared architecture between health and longevity. The informed-GWAS study makes the reason for the thinness explicit: in an ordinary analysis of its two long-lived cohorts only APOE/TOMM40 passed a 10% FDR, and it took borrowing power from 14 disease and trait GWAS meta-analyses to recover CDKN2B/ANRIL, ABO and SH2B3/ATXN2. Meanwhile the heritability the search is aimed at is itself smaller than assumed, well under 10% once assortative mating is modelled, so most of the missing signal was never there.

items.question: What two demographic observations did the 2016 Nature analysis use to argue that human lifespan has a fixed limit?
items.answer: First, that improvements in survival with age tend to DECLINE after age 100, so the gains that keep raising life expectancy do not extend into the extreme ages. Second, that the age at death of the world's oldest person has not increased since the 1990s. The authors set this against the background they acknowledge: an ongoing reduction in old-age mortality, a rising maximum age at death, and evidence from other species that lifespan is flexible and can be raised genetically or pharmacologically. Their conclusion is that maximum human lifespan is fixed and subject to natural constraints.

items.question: What data underpin the 2018 claim of a human mortality plateau, and where does the hazard curve level off?
items.answer: Records for all inhabitants of Italy aged 105 and older between 2009 and 2015, born 1896-1910, a total of 3836 documented cases. Hazard rates estimated from these data were level, essentially constant beyond age 105. The authors emphasise that their estimates are free from the aggregation artifacts that limited earlier studies, and present the result as the best evidence to date for extreme-age mortality plateaus in humans, which bears directly on whether there is a biological limit to lifespan and on evolutionary accounts of human longevity.

items.question: Late-life mortality deceleration is often taken as evidence that ageing slows or stops in extreme old age. What is the competing explanation?
items.answer: Demographic error. Age estimation and cohort blending errors introduced at rates BELOW 1 in 10,000 are sufficient to produce late-life mortality deceleration and plateaus, and in humans the observed error rates of birth and death registration predict the magnitude of the deceleration actually seen. Correcting for these error sources with a mixed linear model eliminates both the deceleration and the late-life plateaus without invoking any biological or evolutionary mechanism. The implications drawn are that models built to explain the deceleration were fitted to an error distribution, that ageing does not slow or stop in old age in humans, and that there is a finite limit to human longevity.

items.question: Hur mycket längre kan vi räkna med att leva under det här århundradet, enligt den demografiska analysen från 2024?
items.answer: Betydligt mindre än under 1900-talet. Analysen använde överlevnadsmått ur nationell dödsstatistik 1990-2019 för de åtta länder som har de mest långlivade befolkningarna, nämligen Australien, Frankrike, Italien, Japan, Sydkorea, Spanien, Sverige och Schweiz, samt Hongkong och USA. Under 1900-talet steg den förväntade livslängden vid födseln med omkring 30 år i höginkomstländerna, men sedan 1990 har förbättringstakten bromsat in. Samtidigt ökade motståndet mot ytterligare förbättringar, medan ojämlikheten i livslängd minskade och dödligheten komprimerades. Författarna beräknar att andelen som når 100 år knappast överstiger 15% för kvinnor och 5% för män, och drar slutsatsen att radikal livsförlängning är osannolik under 2000-talet om inte själva åldrandeprocessen kan bromsas påtagligt.

items.question: What is the compression of morbidity, as Fries originally set it out in 1980, and what number did he attach to the ideal average lifespan?
items.answer: The argument is that average length of life had risen from 47 to 73 years over the century while maximum lifespan had not increased, so survival curves were becoming ever more rectangular; 80% of years of life lost to non-traumatic premature death had been eliminated and most premature deaths were by then from chronic diseases of later life. Fries calculated an ideal average lifespan of approximately 85 years. His proposal was that if chronic illness can be postponed by changes in lifestyle, and the physiologic and psychologic markers of ageing modified, then the average age at first infirmity rises, the morbidity curve also becomes rectangular, and adult vigour extends into a FIXED lifespan, compressing senescence into a short period near the end.

items.question: Has the compression of morbidity actually happened at population scale? What did the GBD 2023 analysis of the morbidity gap find?
items.answer: No; the gap widened almost everywhere. Defining the morbidity gap as life expectancy minus healthy life expectancy across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, the global gap rose from 8.8 years (95% UI 6.7-11.2) to 10.7 (8.2-13.7), an increase of 1.9 years or 21.9%, with point estimates showing widening in 203 of 204 countries. The share of life spent in poor health rose from 13.6% to 14.5%. Age-specific gaps widened across the adult life course rather than concentrating in the final years, gaps were LARGEST in the high-SDI quintile and smallest in the low-SDI quintile, and a few chronic largely non-fatal causes dominated: musculoskeletal disorders led by low back pain, depressive and anxiety disorders, age-related hearing loss, falls and other non-communicable diseases together made up 57.4% of unhealthy years in 2023.

items.question: Why is reporting only the average number of years spent in poor health insufficient for testing compression of morbidity, and what did the Danish hospitalisation analysis show once variation was included?
items.answer: Because Fries framed compression in terms of VARIATION in age at morbidity onset, not the mean, and studies routinely report only the average years in an unhealthy state. Using incidence of first hospitalisation after age 60 in Danish population registers over 1987-2014, the average age at first admission of two or more days rose from 67.8 years (95% CI 67.7-67.9) to 69.5 (69.4-69.6) in men and from 69.1 to 70.5 in women, so onset shifted to older ages. But the coefficient of variation in age at first admission also rose, from 9.1% to 9.9% in men and from 10.3% to 10.6% in women. Populations are therefore ageing in better health than before while becoming more heterogeneous in how they do so, which average measures cannot capture and which pensions, social care and health services have to plan for.

items.question: What does the study of supercentenarians show about the relationship between healthspan and lifespan at the extreme of survival?
items.answer: That they converge. Following 104 supercentenarians (110-119), 430 semisupercentenarians (105-109), 884 centenarians (100-104), 343 nonagenarians and 436 controls prospectively for an average of 3 years, the older the age group the LATER the onset of cancer, cardiovascular disease, dementia and stroke, and of cognitive and functional decline. Hazard ratios for these individual diseases became progressively smaller in older groups, and the relative period of time spent with disease was lower with increasing age group. As the approximate limit of human lifespan is reached in supercentenarians, compression of morbidity is generally observed, so healthspan approximates lifespan in these individuals.

items.question: Är det sant att diabetiker som tar metformin lever längre än folk utan diabetes?
items.answer: Det är vad en brittisk registerstudie fann, men den kan inte bära den tolkning som brukar läggas på den. Ur Clinical Practice Research Datalink valdes 78 241 personer med typ 2-diabetes som fick metformin i monoterapi, 12 222 som fick sulfonylurea, och 90 463 matchade personer utan diabetes, med sammanlagt 503 384 personår och 7 498 dödsfall. Med metformingruppen som referens var den justerade mediantiden till död 15% kortare hos de matchade icke-diabetikerna (survival time ratio 0.85; 95% KI 0.81-0.90) och 38% kortare hos sulfonylureagruppen (0.62; 0.58-0.66). Men detta är retrospektiva observationsdata, inte en randomiserad prövning: den som får metformin i monoterapi är den som har mildare sjukdom och tål läkemedlet, och den jämförelsen kan inte skiljas från läkemedlets egen effekt. Författarna formulerar också slutsatsen försiktigt, som att resultatet antyder att metformin kan ge nytta även utan diabetes.

items.question: What was the primary objective of the first senolytic trial in Alzheimer's disease, and how many patients did it involve?
items.answer: The primary objective was to evaluate whether dasatinib and quercetin penetrate the central nervous system, assessed by analysis of cerebrospinal fluid collected at baseline and after 12 weeks of intermittent treatment. It was an open-label vanguard study in five older adults with early-stage Alzheimer's disease. Secondary measures covered target engagement plus cognitive, functional and physical outcomes, and preliminary safety, feasibility and efficacy data. The stated purpose was to inform the design of a subsequent randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicentre phase II trial, not to establish efficacy.

items.question: Why did CALERIE need an elaborate behavioural intervention rather than simply instructing people to eat 25% less, and what did the design involve?
items.answer: Because sustaining a defined restriction for two years in free-living non-obese people is the hard part of the experiment, and CALERIE was the first investigation of long-term caloric restriction on the ageing process in non-obese humans. 220 healthy volunteers with BMI at least 22 and under 28 were recruited across three sites from May 2007 and randomised 2:1 to restriction or an ad libitum diet. The intervention combined a mixed schedule of group and individual sessions, a meal-provision phase exposing participants to various diets, personal digital assistants for monitoring intake, portion-estimation training, tailored treatment through a computer tracking system, toolbox strategies and algorithms, and coverage of nutrition and behavioural topics, several of which were novel methods for achieving restriction.

items.question: Why is it difficult to run a clinical trial of an anti-ageing intervention, in terms of what you would measure?
items.answer: Because the endpoint problem has no settled answer. Trials that use clinical endpoints such as disease diagnosis or death need biomarkers to show the intervention is acting on the underlying biology long before enough events accumulate, but there is no standard set of biomarkers of ageing for clinical trials. The TAME Biomarkers Workgroup screened 258 candidates against reliability and feasibility, relevance to ageing, prediction of mortality and of clinical and functional outcomes, and responsiveness to intervention, and arrived at a short list of nine blood markers while noting the scarcity of well-vetted biomarkers reflecting biological hallmarks of ageing. The candidate composite outcome measures fare no better: eleven telomere, epigenetic-clock and biomarker-composite quantifications applied to the same 964 people agreed poorly with each other, and only some related to functional outcomes, with modest effect sizes.

items.question: What is the geroscience hypothesis, in the terms its own proponents use?
items.answer: That mammalian ageing can be delayed by genetic, dietary and pharmacologic means, and that because ageing is the greatest risk factor for the majority of chronic diseases driving morbidity and mortality, targeting ageing itself should postpone many diseases at once; the practical corollary is that geroscience research aimed at extending human healthspan must be expanded as the elderly population grows. The companion framing from the same period is historical: identification of gene variants extending lifespan in multicellular model organisms about thirty years ago gave the biology of ageing its scientific credibility, and the field is described as reaching an inflection point with medical, commercial and societal consequences.

items.question: Varför lever kvinnor längre än män?
items.answer: En metaanalys ställde frågan tvärtom: beror skillnaden på faktorer som ger kvinnor låg dödlighet, eller på faktorer som ger män hög? Den undersökte variationen i dödlighet, alltså spännvidden i dödstal mellan olika delgrupper, i 72 empiriska studier med 146 totaleffekter och 1 718 enskilda effekter för 21 riskfaktorer. I 85% av totaleffekterna och tre fjärdedelar av de enskilda effekterna var variationen större bland män än bland kvinnor, även med hänsyn tagen till männens högre dödlighet överlag; ser man på de direkta skillnaderna i variation är siffrorna 92% respektive 82%. Fall där kvinnor har större variation är sällsynta undantag och dyker främst upp i de allra äldsta åldersgrupperna. Slutsatsen är att skillnaden i förväntad livslängd till stor del drivs av vissa mansgrupper med mycket hög dödlighet, kopplade främst till socioekonomiska förhållanden, och att folkhälsoarbetet därför bör riktas mot dessa grupper.

items.question: Lay out the maximum-lifespan debate as the primary literature actually leaves it: what is claimed, what is contested, and what is agreed.
items.answer: Three positions have to be held at once. The 2016 analysis argued for a fixed limit from two observations: survival improvements decline after age 100, and the age at death of the world's oldest person has not risen since the 1990s. The 2018 Italian study cut against that by showing, in 3836 documented cases aged 105 and over born 1896-1910, hazard rates that are essentially constant beyond 105, which is what a plateau rather than a hard wall looks like, and which the authors present as free of the aggregation artifacts of earlier work. The same year a third analysis showed that age-estimation and cohort-blending errors at rates below 1 in 10,000 are enough to manufacture exactly such plateaus, that observed birth and death registration error rates predict the magnitude seen in humans, and that correcting for them removes the plateau entirely, concluding that ageing does not slow in old age and that longevity is finite. What is not contested is that the record has not moved and that improvement at extreme ages has stalled; what is contested is whether the flat hazard at 105-plus is biology or bad paperwork, and it is a data-quality question before it is a biological one.
